troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 5246 FMI 31 be cleared at the truck without a shop visit?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Not reliably. A key-off cycle may temporarily change the code status, but the inducement restriction will return if the root cause faults are still active. Proper resolution requires repairing the underlying aftertreatment problem and then using Cummins Insite to reset the inducement counter through the approved procedure.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is this code specific to Cummins, or does it appear on other engine brands?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: SPN 5246 is a J1939-defined SPN, so other manufacturers can use it �?but the exact implementation, inducement thresholds, and reset procedures differ by brand. On Cummins CM2350 engines, the inducement system is documented through Cummins Insite and QuickServe. Detroit, Volvo, and other brands have their own inducement strategies.

troubleshooting_faq.question: What happens if the truck is driven indefinitely with this code active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The restriction typically remains in place until a proper reset is performed. Some calibrations escalate the severity of the restriction over additional distance. Running the SCR system in a degraded state for extended periods can also accelerate catalyst wear.

field_evidence.excerpt: The 2012 International Durastar MaxxForce DT can experience a no-start condition indicated by the diagnostic trouble code SPN 51 FMI 11. This no-start issue can stem from faults related to the crankshaft position sensor or its electrical connections. Additionally, injector harness faults and sensor communication errors, including codes SPN 2798 and 2797 with FMC 3 and 4, may contribute to this condition by affecting injector circuits and wiring. field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Freightliner Cascadia equipped with the DD15 engine may display the SPN 70 FMI 19 engine code, which relates to a turbocharger boost pressure fault. This problem is commonly associated with issues affecting the engine's turbocharger system. Such turbocharger boost pressure faults can stem from several causes. These issues can lead to engine derate or reduced performance if not addressed promptly. field_evidence.excerpt: The SPN 107 fault code is commonly associated with issues involving the engine coolant temperature sensor or its circuit. Vehicles displaying this code often experience frequent engine misfires and sensor communication errors that affect overall engine performance. This fault can stem from damage or loose connections in the sensor wiring, which may result in incorrect temperature readings. Such inaccuracies in temperature data can contribute directly to engine misfires and other operational problems. To address the SPN 107 fault code, it is advisable to perform several checks: Inspect the wiring of the engine coolant temperature sensor for any signs of damage or loose connections. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 210: Transmission Oil Pressure (Fluid Pressure Sensor)
dd_procedures.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with a Fluid Pressure Sensor (FPS) to monitor lubricant oil pressure. The transmission oil pump provides the supply oil for the lubrication system. The FPS taps into the lubrication system and provides a pressure input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM). The TCM monitors the pressure input to verify the transmission is properly filled with oil to lubricate the transmission. The FPS is mounted externally and connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 210: Line Pressure
dd_procedures.overview: The Procision transmission is equipped with a Triple Pressure Sensor (TPS) that senses oil pressures and sump oil temperature within the transmission hydraulic system and provides input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM). The supply oil to the Actuation Control Manifold (ACM) controls all hydraulic operations. The pressure of the supply oil, or Line Pressure, is critical for proper transmission operation. The TPS is mounted to the ACM and is connected to the TCM through the Transmission Harness.

troubleshooting_faq.question: What is the correct fluid level check procedure for an Allison transmission?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Allison transmissions require a hot-check procedure: the vehicle must be on level ground, the engine running, the transmission warm and in Park or Neutral, and the dipstick or sight glass must be read within a few seconds of pulling the stick. Checking cold or with the engine off gives an inaccurate level reading. Allison's service documentation and the sticker on the dipstick tube typically describe the model-specific procedure.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can Allison SPN 127 FMI 1 be confused with Eaton SPN 127 FMI 1?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The SPN and FMI numbers are identical because both manufacturers follow the J1939 standard, but the transmissions are completely different designs with different diagnostic tools and service procedures. Allison uses DOC; Eaton uses ServiceRanger. Always confirm which transmission brand is installed before selecting a service path.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does this code affect the PTO on a vocational truck?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: In some cases, yes. Allison transmissions equipped with PTO provisions depend on main pressure to engage the PTO. Low main pressure can prevent PTO engagement or cause inconsistent PTO operation. If a fleet truck is also reporting PTO problems alongside this code, both issues likely share the same hydraulic root cause.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton Transmission SPN 127 FMI 1 �?Transmission Oil Pressure Below Normal | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Which fluid does Eaton specify for automated transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton specifies approved fluids for each transmission family in the respective service literature. The correct fluid grade and change interval vary between the Gen 3 UltraShift PLUS and the Endurant HD. Using the wrong grade �?particularly a lighter fluid than specified �?can result in chronic low-pressure codes. Always verify against the Eaton service document for the specific transmission.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 127 FMI 1 cause the transmission to lock in a gear?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: In some cases, yes. If the TCM determines that pressure is too low to safely execute a gear change, it may inhibit shifts to avoid a disengaged or partially-engaged gear. The transmission will attempt to hold the most recently confirmed gear. How aggressively it inhibits depends on ECM calibration and how far pressure has dropped.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is there a hydraulic filter that should be checked alongside this code?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton AMTs have an internal transmission filter that is typically serviced at fluid change intervals. A clogged filter restricts flow to the pump and can contribute to pressure concerns. If the fluid service history is unknown, a filter inspection is worth including in the diagnostic process.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Allison Transmission SPN 177 FMI 0 �?Transmission Fluid Temperature Above Normal | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the transmission recover from an overtemperature event without damage?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: A single, brief overtemperature event that clears quickly may not cause lasting damage, especially in a transmission with good fluid and recent service. Repeated events or sustained high temperatures accelerate fluid and seal degradation. Allison DOC's thermal event history can help a technician assess whether the transmission has experienced chronic overheating.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does adding a transmission cooler eliminate this code?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: An external auxiliary cooler can reduce operating temperatures in high-demand applications and may prevent the code from recurring. However, if the code was originally caused by a restricted existing cooler or a low fluid level, adding a new cooler without fixing the root cause may only partially address the problem.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How often should transmission fluid be changed in a vocational Allison application?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Allison specifies fluid change intervals based on application severity. High-cycle vocational applications �?refuse, transit, severe on/off highway �?use shorter intervals than on-highway linehaul applications. Consult Allison's service documentation for the TranSynd or approved fluid intervals for the specific series and application. Using fluid beyond its service life contributes to thermal degradation.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton UltraShift SPN 177 FMI 0 �?Transmission Fluid Temperature Above Normal | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What fluid does the Eaton UltraShift use?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton UltraShift transmissions require Eaton-approved transmission fluid, typically a 50-weight mineral gear oil meeting Eaton PS-164 or equivalent for older units, and synthetic fluid for newer PLUS-generation units. Confirm the fluid specification in the Eaton maintenance guide for the specific transmission model and generation.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does the Eaton UltraShift have an auxiliary cooler option for vocational applications?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. Eaton offers an auxiliary cooler option for UltraShift transmissions in demanding duty cycles �?heavy construction, refuse, or extreme mountain grades �?where the standard cooler circuit cannot maintain acceptable fluid temperatures. An auxiliary cooler is mounted in the air stream and supplements the engine coolant-based transmission cooler.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How does SPN 177 FMI 0 differ from FMI 16 on the Eaton UltraShift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: FMI 0 indicates temperature is above normal range �?a measurement that exceeds the normal operating spec. FMI 16 indicates an above-normal moderate-severity condition on some J1939 implementations, which may represent an earlier-stage warning threshold. In practice, both FMI values indicate the transmission is running hotter than intended and require the same diagnostic approach: investigate the cooling circuit and fluid condition.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton UltraShift SPN 177 FMI 16 �?Transmission Fluid Temperature High | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What transmission fluid specification does the Eaton UltraShift require?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton specifies PS-386 approved fluids for UltraShift and Fuller Advantage transmissions. This includes several synthetic and conventional transmission lubricants from major suppliers. Using a non-approved fluid can affect thermal protection and shift quality. Verify the correct specification using Eaton's fluid guide for the specific transmission model.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can driving habits cause SPN 177 FMI 16 on an Eaton UltraShift in a vocational application?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. In vocational applications such as construction or refuse trucks, frequent stops with heavy loads and high launch torque demands generate significant heat. If the cooler is sized adequately but the duty cycle is exceptionally demanding, the fluid may still reach the warning threshold during peak operation. Operating parameters within the application's rated duty cycle should not cause chronic temperature faults.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How often should the transmission fluid be changed on an Eaton UltraShift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton specifies fluid change intervals based on application and fluid type �?typically every 250,000 to 500,000 miles for approved synthetic fluids in standard applications, with shorter intervals for severe duty. High-temperature events can accelerate fluid degradation and may warrant an earlier change. Eaton ServiceRanger tracks fluid temperature history and can flag conditions that suggest the fluid has been thermally stressed.

oem_troubleshooting.title: ZF AS-Tronic / TraXon SPN 177 FMI 16 �?Transmission Fluid Temperature High | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What ZF transmission fluid specification should be used in an AS-Tronic or TraXon?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: ZF specifies TE-ML 02, 12, or 16 approved fluids for AS-Tronic and TraXon transmissions depending on the application. Always verify the correct specification using the ZF lubrication table for the specific transmission model and application �?using an incorrect fluid grade can affect thermal protection and shift behavior.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the ZF TraXon transmission reduce power or limit shifting when SPN 177 FMI 16 is active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. The ZF TCU may modify its shift strategy �?for example, skipping shift points to reduce clutch slip heat �?when fluid temperature exceeds the warning threshold. This is a protective response designed to reduce heat generation and prevent the temperature from escalating to the critical shutdown level.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the transmission cooler on a ZF AS-Tronic part of the engine coolant circuit?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes, on most heavy-duty truck applications the ZF transmission cooler is integrated into the engine coolant circuit �?hot transmission fluid passes through a heat exchanger cooled by engine coolant. This means that if the engine is running hot (elevated coolant temperature), the transmission cooler becomes less effective, which can contribute to high transmission fluid temperature.

field_evidence.title: 2014 Cascadia Evolution DT12 Transmission Code SPN 523 FMI 19 Explained
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Cascadia Evolution equipped with the DT12 transmission can experience drivability issues linked to sensor faults and communication errors. One specific problem identified by technicians is the transmission code SPN 523 FMI 19. This code indicates a fault with the transmission output speed sensor in the DT12 system. Such a fault can stem from several factors related to the sensor and its associated components. To address SPN 523 FMI 19, it is important to check the sensor wiring harness for any signs of damage or corrosion that could disrupt signal transmission. Inspecting the sensor itself for debris or misalignment is also crucial. Often, cleaning or replacing the sensor can resolve the issue. Beyond the sensor, verifying the transmission control module connections is recommended

The DC/DC Converter is energized only in ePTO mode so it can charge the 12-volt battery system. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) operates the Motor/Generator to power the transmission mounted PTO. If the High-Voltage Batteries get low, the HCM will start the engine with the Motor/Generator or the standard 12-Volt System. dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 – EGR Valve Fault Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 – EGR Valve Position Fault (Meaning & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 indicates an issue with EGR valve position. This code appears when the EGR valve is not responding correctly to commanded position signals.
Symptoms
Check engine light illuminated
Rough idle
Reduced fuel efficiency
Increased exhaust smoke
Possible aftertreatment warnings
Cause
This fault is commonly caused by a sticking EGR valve, carbon buildup, faulty actuator, wiring issues, or inaccurate position sensor readings.
Can You Keep Driving?
Driving may be possible temporarily, but unresolved EGR valve issues can lead to additional emissions faults and engine derate.
Recommended Action
Inspect the EGR valve for carbon buildup and proper movement. Test actuator operation and verify sensor readings. Clean or replace faulty components as needed.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 mean?
 
SPN 2659 FMI 0 indicates that the EGR valve position is not responding correctly to commanded signals from the engine control module.
 
 
What causes SPN 2659 FMI 0?
 
Common causes include carbon buildup, a sticking EGR valve, faulty actuator, damaged wiring, or a failed position sensor.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 2659 FMI 0?
 
Driving may be possible temporarily, but unresolved EGR valve faults can lead to emissions issues and possible engine derate.
 
 
Will SPN 2659 FMI 0 cause reduced power?
 
Yes. Improper EGR valve operation can trigger engine protection strategies, including power reduction.
 
 
How do I fix SPN 2659 FMI 0?
 
Inspect the EGR valve for carbon buildup, test actuator movement, verify wiring integrity, and replace faulty components as needed.

SPN 3719 (DPF)
SPN 1569 (Derate)

Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 – EGR Valve Position Fault (Meaning & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 indicates an issue with EGR valve position. This code appears when the EGR valve is not responding correctly to commanded position signals.
Symptoms
Check engine light illuminated
Rough idle
Reduced fuel efficiency
Increased exhaust smoke
Possible aftertreatment warnings
Cause
This fault is commonly caused by a sticking EGR valve, carbon buildup, faulty actuator, wiring issues, or inaccurate position sensor readings.

Driving may be possible temporarily, but unresolved EGR valve issues can lead to additional emissions faults and engine derate.

Inspect the EGR valve for carbon buildup, test actuator movement, verify wiring integrity, and replace faulty components as needed.

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3250 FMI 16 – DPF Differential Pressure High
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3250 FMI 16 – DPF Differential Pressure High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3250 FMI 16 indicates that the pressure difference across the Diesel Particulate Filter has exceeded the acceptable operating threshold. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and signals that exhaust flow through the DPF is being restricted, which directly impacts engine performance and will trigger derate conditions if not addressed promptly.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF warning light illuminated 
Reduced engine power 
Engine derate condition possible Increased exhaust back pressure 
Regeneration cycles may be more frequent 
Black smoke from exhaust possible
Cause
This code triggers when the differential pressure sensor detects a pressure drop across the DPF exceeding the maximum threshold. Common causes include:
Heavily soot loaded DPF restricting exhaust flow 
High ash accumulation inside the DPF 
Failed or incomplete regeneration cycles 
Clogged or damaged DPF substrate 
Faulty differential pressure sensor or blocked sensor lines 
Engine burning excessive oil accelerating ash buildup 
Collapsed or damaged DPF internal structure
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but high differential pressure indicates severely restricted exhaust flow which reduces engine performance and can cause damage. A regeneration should be attempted immediately. If pressure remains high after a successful regen the DPF likely needs professional cleaning or replacement.
Recommended Action
Attempt a parked regeneration to reduce soot load and pressure. If the differential pressure remains high after a successful regen, inspect the sensor lines for blockages before condemning the DPF. If lines are clear the DPF should be removed for professional cleaning or inspection. Also check for excessive oil consumption that may be contributing to rapid ash accumulation.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3250 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the pressure difference across the DPF has exceeded the maximum acceptable threshold, indicating the filter is restricting exhaust flow due to soot, ash, or physical damage.
 
 
What causes SPN 3250 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are a heavily soot or ash loaded DPF, failed regeneration cycles, a clogged or damaged filter substrate, or a faulty differential pressure sensor.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3250 FMI 16?
 
Short distances may be possible but high back pressure from a restricted DPF will reduce engine performance and can cause damage if ignored. Attempt a parked regen as soon as safely possible.
 
 
Will SPN 3250 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Excessive differential pressure across the DPF will cause the ECM to trigger derate conditions to protect the engine from damage caused by high exhaust back pressure.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3250 FMI 16?
 
Perform a parked regeneration to reduce soot load. If pressure remains elevated after regen check the sensor lines for blockages then have the DPF professionally cleaned or replaced if needed.

SPN 3480 FMI 16

field_evidence.excerpt: The Detroit DD15 engine can experience issues related to the DOC inlet pressure sensor, specifically triggering the fault code SPN 3609/FMI 4. These problems often stem from sensor wiring shorts and inaccurate pressure readings from the Diesel Oxidation Catalyst (DOC) inlet sensor. Accurate readings from the DOC inlet pressure sensor are critical for the engine's emissions control system performance. Sensor wiring shorts or faults can cause erroneous pressure measurements, leading to the activation of fault codes and potential engine performance concerns. field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Freightliner Cascadia equipped with the DD15 engine may display the SPN 70 FMI 19 engine code, which relates to a turbocharger boost pressure fault. This problem is commonly associated with issues affecting the engine's turbocharger system. Such turbocharger boost pressure faults can stem from several causes. Notably, a faulty Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor may trigger this code. Additionally, boost leaks in hoses or intercooler connections and a malfunctioning wastegate actuator contribute to this problem. These issues can lead to engine derate or reduced performance if not addressed promptly. field_evidence.excerpt: The 2017 Cascadia DD15 engine can experience specific issues indicated by engine fault codes SPN-3510 and SPN-723. These codes commonly appear following modifications to the Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) system, such as a DEF delete or injector repairs. Code SPN-3510 points to a sensor supply voltage problem, which often arises from faults in the wiring or the sensor itself. Meanwhile, SPN-723 relates to errors in the engine speed sensor signal. Both issues can be linked to disruptions in sensor wiring harnesses or connectors located near the Engine Control Module (ECM). It is important to check whether any programming resets have reversed the DEF delete modifications, as such reversions can trigger these fault codes. field_evidence.excerpt: Trucks experiencing frequent sensor communication errors and intermittent engine control module (ECM) faults can face reduced reliability in diagnostics. Two common fault codes encountered are SPN 3610 FMI 2 and SPN 102 FMI 18, each indicating specific issues within the vehicle's sensor and ECM systems. SPN 3610 FMI 2 signals a sensor data invalid or out-of-range error. This fault often stems from problems with the sensor itself or its associated wiring. Similarly, SPN 102 FMI 18 points to an internal failure within the engine control module or a loss of communication with this critical component. dd_procedures.title: SPN 4766 FMI 31 – DPF Active Regeneration Inhibited
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
SPN 4766 FMI 31 – DPF Active Regeneration Inhibited
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4766 FMI 31 indicates that the DPF active regeneration process is being prevented from initiating or completing due to a system condition or fault. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the ECM has determined that conditions are not safe or suitable for active regeneration to proceed. With regeneration blocked soot will continue to accumulate in the DPF leading to progressively more severe fault codes.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or regen warning light illuminated 
Active regeneration not initiating 
DPF soot load continuing to rise 
Engine derate possible as soot accumulates 
Regen inhibit indicator may be illuminated on dash
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM determines one or more conditions are preventing active regeneration from proceeding. Common causes include:
Regen inhibit switch manually activated by driver 
Active fault codes preventing regeneration from initiating 
Low fuel level preventing regen from starting 
Engine operating conditions outside regen parameters 
Faulty regen related sensor preventing ECM from approving regen 
Parking brake not applied during attempted parked regen 
Multiple active fault codes creating inhibit conditions 
HC dosing system fault preventing regen from being approved
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but with active regeneration inhibited soot will continue to build in the DPF. If the inhibit condition is not resolved the DPF will reach critical soot levels triggering more severe derate conditions. Identify and resolve the inhibit cause as soon as possible.
Recommended Action
First check if the regen inhibit switch is activated and turn it off if so. Check fuel level and top up if low. Clear any active fault codes that may be creating inhibit conditions and attempt a parked regeneration. If regeneration remains inhibited have the HC dosing system, regen related sensors, and ECM conditions evaluated by a qualified diesel technician.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4766 FMI 31 mean?
 
It means the ECM is preventing active DPF regeneration from proceeding due to a system condition or fault that makes regeneration unsafe or impossible under current conditions.
 
 
What causes SPN 4766 FMI 31?
 
The most common causes are the regen inhibit switch being active, low fuel level, active fault codes creating inhibit conditions, or a faulty sensor preventing the ECM from approving regeneration.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4766 FMI 31?
 
Short distances may be possible but with regeneration inhibited soot will accumulate and more severe DPF faults will follow. Resolve the inhibit condition as soon as possible.
 
 
Will SPN 4766 FMI 31 cause a derate?
 
Not immediately but as soot accumulates from blocked regeneration more severe DPF soot codes will trigger derate conditions.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4766 FMI 31?
 
Identify and resolve the condition inhibiting regeneration — check the inhibit switch, fuel level, and any active fault codes. Once the inhibit condition is cleared and a successful active regeneration completes the code should clear.
 
 
Related codes

SPN 3713 FMI 16 
SPN 3713 FMI 18 
SPN 3719 FMI 0 
SPN 3556 FMI 16

This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

SPN_3058.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3363 FMI 16 – DEF Pump Pressure High
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3363 FMI 16 – DEF Pump Pressure High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3363 FMI 16 indicates that the DEF pump is generating pressure above the acceptable operating range. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and signals a problem within the DEF supply system that can prevent proper dosing and lead to SCR system faults and engine derate if not resolved.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate possible 
DEF system operating abnormally 
Possible DEF leaks from pressurized components
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects DEF pump pressure exceeding the specified threshold. Common causes include:
Blocked or restricted DEF return line 
Clogged DEF filter Faulty DEF pressure relief valve 
Failed DEF pump delivering excessive pressure 
Pinched or kinked DEF lines restricting flow 
Faulty DEF pressure sensor giving false high readings
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but excessive pressure in the DEF system can cause damage to lines, fittings, and the dosing injector. Address this fault promptly to avoid more costly repairs to the aftertreatment system.
Recommended Action
Start by inspecting the DEF filter and replacing it if clogged. Check the DEF return line for blockages, kinks, or restrictions. If the filter and lines are clear, have the DEF pump, pressure relief valve, and pressure sensor inspected by a qualified diesel technician.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3363 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the DEF pump is generating pressure above the acceptable operating range, which can disrupt proper DEF dosing and damage system components.
 
 
What causes SPN 3363 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are a clogged DEF filter, a blocked DEF return line, a faulty pressure relief valve, or a failing DEF pump producing excessive pressure.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3363 FMI 16?
 
Short distances may be possible but continued operation with excessive DEF system pressure risks damaging lines, fittings, and the dosing injector.
 
 
Will SPN 3363 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
It can if the high pressure condition prevents proper DEF dosing and the SCR system cannot meet emissions thresholds as a result.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3363 FMI 16?
 
Inspect and replace the DEF filter, check the return line for restrictions, and have the DEF pump and pressure relief valve tested. Once pressure returns to normal operating range the code should clear.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 58: Output Shaft Speed Sensor
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with electronic speed sensors. The Input Shaft, Main Shaft and Output Shaft Speed Sensors are used to calculate gear ratios within the transmission. The Input Shaft Speed Sensor measures the rotational speed of the Input Shaft, taken from the upper countershaft drive gear. The Main Shaft Speed Sensor measures the rotational speed of the transmission gearing exiting the main case, taken from the auxiliary upper countershaft gear. The Output Shaft Speed Sensor measures the rotational speed and direction of the output shaft, taken from the Tone Wheel.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 375: Output Speed
dd_procedures.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with speed sensors to monitor input, Countershaft and output speeds. The speed sensors provide rotational speed inputs to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) to verify clutch operation and calculate gear ratios. The Output Speed Sensor measures the rotational speed and direction of the Planetary Output Shaft Assembly. The Output Speed Sensor is mounted externally and connects at the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) Housing. The 3-Way Output Speed Sensor Connector connects to the TCM at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Will cleaning the sensor fix SPN 191 FMI 8 permanently?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: If metallic debris was the cause, cleaning the sensor face can restore normal operation. However, rapid re-accumulation of metallic debris can indicate abnormal internal wear. Change the transmission fluid and inspect the magnetic drain plug material if the debris was significant.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 191 FMI 8 affect the truck's ABS system?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Possibly. Some vehicles use the transmission output shaft speed as a secondary input for ABS and stability control modules. An erratic transmission speed signal could create a disagreement between systems. If ABS codes appear alongside this code, the transmission sensor should be confirmed first before assuming ABS hardware is at fault.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does this code appear in Eaton Endurant HD transmissions the same way as older UltraShift models?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The SPN and FMI are consistent across Eaton automated transmission families that use J1939 reporting. ServiceRanger is the correct tool for all Eaton AMT models; some model-specific diagnostic procedures differ between Gen 3 AutoShift/UltraShift PLUS and the Endurant HD, so use the appropriate service documentation.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton UltraShift SPN 191 FMI 8 �?Output Shaft Speed Sensor Erratic | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the output shaft speed sensor on the Eaton UltraShift Plus the same as on the older Fuller automated transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The UltraShift Plus and the earlier Fuller AutoShift use similar speed sensor architectures �?a magnetic pickup or Hall-effect sensor reading a tone wheel �?but the specific sensor part numbers, tone wheel configurations, and mounting details may differ between transmission generations. ServiceRanger part look-up or the Roadranger service portal can confirm the correct part for the specific transmission model.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can a worn transmission output seal affect the tone wheel and cause SPN 191 FMI 8 on the Eaton UltraShift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: A worn output seal can allow lubricant to contaminate the sensor area, which may foul the sensor face and produce erratic readings. Inspecting the sensor for oil contamination alongside checking the tone wheel condition is worthwhile during diagnosis.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How does the Eaton UltraShift use output shaft speed data compared to vehicle speed from the ABS?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The Eaton UltraShift TCM uses its own output shaft speed sensor for primary shift control. It may also receive vehicle speed data from the ABS via J1939 as a reference. When both sources are available and agree, shift control is optimal. When the transmission output sensor is faulted, the TCM may attempt to use the J1939 vehicle speed as a fallback, but this depends on the specific transmission generation and calibration.

oem_troubleshooting.title: ZF AS-Tronic / TraXon SPN 191 FMI 8 �?Output Shaft Speed Sensor Erratic | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What is the difference between the ZF AS-Tronic and ZF TraXon in terms of speed sensor design?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The ZF TraXon is the current-generation automated transmission platform that superseded the AS-Tronic for new applications. Both use output shaft speed sensors for shift control, but the sensor types, connector formats, and tone wheel designs differ between generations. ZF Testman covers both platforms with specific procedures for each model.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the ZF TraXon transmission enter a safe mode if SPN 191 FMI 8 is active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. If the TCM cannot determine vehicle speed accurately from the output sensor and no alternative speed reference is available, the TraXon may restrict certain operating modes or gear ranges as a protective measure. The specific response depends on the severity of the signal fault and the transmission calibration.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is ZF Testman or WABCO Toolbox required to diagnose SPN 191 FMI 8 on the ZF AS-Tronic?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: While the fault code itself is readable with any J1939-capable scan tool, ZF Testman provides the live data parameters �?output shaft speed, sensor signal quality, and bidirectional tests �?needed to effectively characterize the fault. Generic scan tools typically cannot access these specific ZF live data channels.

field_evidence.title: Cummins ISX Fuel Issue Diagnosis for SPN 974 FMI 3 and SPN 1483 FMI 9
field_evidence.excerpt: The Cummins ISX engine may experience fuel delivery failures that lead to engine shutdowns. SPN 974 FMI 3 indicates that the engine is detecting low fuel pressure. dd_procedures.title: SPN 3509 FMI 16 – DEF Concentration Out of Range
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3509 FMI 16 – DEF Concentration Out of Range (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3509 FMI 16 indicates that the DEF fluid concentration is outside the acceptable range. Proper DEF must contain 32.5% urea and 67.5% deionized water. When the ECM detects the concentration is off on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines, the SCR system cannot function correctly and a derate condition will follow.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition 
Reduced vehicle speed 
SCR system performance degraded
Cause
This code triggers when the DEF quality sensor detects that the urea concentration in the tank does not meet the required 32.5% standard. Common causes include:
Wrong fluid added to DEF tank (water, diesel, or other fluid) 
Poor quality or off-brand DEF with incorrect concentration 
DEF that has degraded due to age or heat exposure 
Contaminated DEF tank Faulty 
DEF quality sensor giving incorrect readings
Can You Keep Driving?
The engine will enter a derate condition fairly quickly with this fault active. The SCR system requires correct DEF concentration to control emissions. Continued operation without addressing the fluid quality will result in progressive power reduction.
Recommended Action
Drain the DEF tank completely and refill with fresh, quality DEF that meets ISO 22241 standards. After refilling, clear the fault codes and allow the system to verify the new fluid. If the code returns after refilling with quality DEF, have the DEF quality sensor inspected and replaced if necessary.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3509 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the DEF fluid in the tank does not have the correct urea concentration and the SCR system cannot operate properly as a result.
 
 
What causes SPN 3509 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are poor quality DEF, wrong fluid added to the DEF tank, degraded DEF, or a faulty DEF quality sensor.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3509 FMI 16?
 
Not recommended. The engine will derate and power will be progressively reduced until the DEF concentration issue is resolved.
 
 
Will SPN 3509 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Incorrect DEF concentration prevents the SCR system from controlling NOx emissions and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3509 FMI 16?
 
Drain and replace the DEF with fresh fluid meeting ISO 22241 standards. Clear the fault codes and allow the system to verify fluid quality. If the code persists with fresh DEF, inspect the DEF quality sensor.

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 4334 FMI 16 – SCR Conversion Efficiency Low
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4334 FMI 16 – SCR Conversion Efficiency Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4334 FMI 16 indicates that the SCR (Selective Catalytic Reduction) system is not converting NOx emissions efficiently enough to meet required thresholds. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and is a moderate severity warning that can escalate to a derate if left unaddressed.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
SCR or DEF warning light illuminated 
Possible reduction in engine performance Increased 
NOx emissions Engine derate may follow if efficiency continues to drop
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects that the SCR catalyst is not reducing NOx at the required efficiency level. Common causes include:
Low quality or contaminated 
DEF fluid Faulty NOx sensor (upstream or downstream) 
Worn or damaged SCR catalyst 
DEF dosing system malfunction 
Exhaust leaks affecting sensor readings
Can You Keep Driving?
Short term driving is possible but this code typically escalates. If the SCR system efficiency continues to fall, the engine will enter a progressive derate. Address this promptly to avoid a more severe code or breakdown.
Recommended Action
Start by checking DEF fluid quality — contaminated or diluted DEF is a very common cause. If DEF quality is good, have the NOx sensors, DEF dosing system, and SCR catalyst inspected by a qualified diesel technician.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4334 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the SCR system is operating but not converting NOx emissions at the required efficiency level, triggering a moderate severity fault.
 
 
What causes SPN 4334 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are poor quality or contaminated DEF, a failing NOx sensor, a worn SCR catalyst, or a DEF dosing system fault.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4334 FMI 16?
 
Limited driving is possible but the code is likely to escalate to a more severe fault and derate if the underlying issue is not addressed.
 
 
Will SPN 4334 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes, if SCR efficiency continues to drop the ECM will trigger progressive derate conditions to reduce emissions output.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4334 FMI 16?
 
Inspect and replace DEF if quality is suspect, then have the NOx sensors and SCR system diagnosed. The code will clear once the system confirms acceptable conversion efficiency.

Detroit Diesel SPN 4334 FMI 16 – SCR Conversion Efficiency Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4334 FMI 16 indicates that the SCR (Selective Catalytic Reduction) system is not converting NOx emissions efficiently enough to meet required thresholds. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and is a moderate severity warning that can escalate to a derate if left unaddressed.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
SCR or DEF warning light illuminated 
Possible reduction in engine performance Increased 
NOx emissions Engine derate may follow if efficiency continues to drop
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects that the SCR catalyst is not reducing NOx at the required efficiency level. Common causes include:
Low quality or contaminated 
DEF fluid Faulty NOx sensor (upstream or downstream) 
Worn or damaged SCR catalyst 
DEF dosing system malfunction 
Exhaust leaks affecting sensor readings
Can You Keep Driving?
Short term driving is possible but this code typically escalates. If the SCR system efficiency continues to fall, the engine will enter a progressive derate. Address this promptly to avoid a more severe code or breakdown.
Recommended Action
Start by checking DEF fluid quality — contaminated or diluted DEF is a very common cause. If DEF quality is good, have the NOx sensors, DEF dosing system, and SCR catalyst inspected by a qualified diesel technician.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4334 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the SCR system is operating but not converting NOx emissions at the required efficiency level, triggering a moderate severity fault.
 
 
What causes SPN 4334 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are poor quality or contaminated DEF, a failing NOx sensor, a worn SCR catalyst, or a DEF dosing system fault.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4334 FMI 16?
 
Limited driving is possible but the code is likely to escalate to a more severe fault and derate if the underlying issue is not addressed.
 
 
Will SPN 4334 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes, if SCR efficiency continues to drop the ECM will trigger progressive derate conditions to reduce emissions output.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4334 FMI 16?
 
Inspect and replace DEF if quality is suspect, then have the NOx sensors and SCR system diagnosed. The code will clear once the system confirms acceptable conversion efficiency.

Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 9 – EGR Valve Position Error (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 9 indicates that the EGR valve position is not matching the commanded position from the ECM. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the exhaust gas recirculation system is not responding correctly, which can affect emissions control, engine performance, and combustion efficiency.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
EGR or emissions warning light illuminated 
Rough idle or unstable engine operation 
Reduced engine performance Engine derate possible Increased 
NOx emissions 
Black smoke from exhaust possible
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects a discrepancy between the commanded EGR valve position and the actual position reported by the valve sensor. Common causes include:
Excessive carbon deposits in the EGR system
Carbon buildup on the EGR valve preventing proper movement
Stuck or seized EGR valve
Failed EGR valve position sensor
Damaged EGR valve actuator motor
Wiring or connector fault at the EGR valve
EGR cooler restriction affecting valve operation
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but an EGR valve position error affects combustion efficiency and emissions control. Engine performance will be impacted and a derate condition may follow if the fault persists. Address this promptly to avoid further carbon buildup or component damage.
Recommended Action
Inspect the EGR valve for carbon buildup and clean if necessary. Check the valve actuator and position sensor for proper operation. Inspect wiring and connectors at the EGR valve for damage or corrosion. If cleaning does not resolve the issue the EGR valve assembly may need to be replaced.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 9 mean?
 
It means the EGR valve is not moving to the position commanded by the ECM, indicating a mechanical, electrical, or carbon buildup issue with the valve or its control system.
 
 
What causes SPN 27 FMI 9?
 
The most common causes are carbon buildup preventing valve movement, a stuck or seized EGR valve, a failed position sensor, or a wiring fault at the valve connector.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 27 FMI 9?
 
Short distances may be possible but EGR valve position errors affect combustion and emissions control. A derate condition may follow if not addressed promptly.
 
 
Will SPN 27 FMI 9 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If the ECM cannot control EGR valve position correctly it will trigger derate conditions to limit emissions and protect the engine.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 27 FMI 9?
 
Clean or replace the EGR valve and inspect the position sensor and wiring. Once the valve responds correctly to ECM commands and position feedback matches commanded values the code should clear.

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 11 – EGR Valve Circuit Fault
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 11 – EGR Valve Circuit Fault
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 11 indicates an electrical circuit fault at the EGR valve. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the ECM has detected an abnormal electrical condition in the EGR valve control circuit, preventing proper valve operation and affecting exhaust gas recirculation control.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
EGR or emissions warning light illuminated 
Rough idle or unstable engine operation 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate possible Increased 
NOx emissions 
May appear alongside other EGR related codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects an electrical fault in the EGR valve circuit. Common causes include:
Open or short circuit in the EGR valve wiring harness 
Corroded or damaged EGR valve connector 
Failed EGR valve solenoid or actuator motor 
Water intrusion at the EGR valve connector 
Chafed or broken wiring between ECM and EGR valve 
Failed ECM output driver for the EGR valve circuit 
Poor ground connection at the EGR valve
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but without proper electrical function the EGR valve cannot be controlled by the ECM. This affects combustion efficiency and emissions control and a derate condition is likely to follow if the fault is not resolved.
Recommended Action
Inspect the EGR valve wiring harness and connector for damage, corrosion, or water intrusion. Check for broken or chafed wires between the ECM and EGR valve. Test the EGR valve solenoid resistance against specification. If wiring and solenoid test correctly have the ECM output circuit evaluated by a qualified diesel technician.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 11 mean?
 
It means the ECM has detected an electrical circuit fault at the EGR valve, preventing proper control of exhaust gas recirculation.
 
 
What causes SPN 27 FMI 11?
 
The most common causes are an open or short circuit in the EGR valve wiring, a corroded connector, water intrusion at the connector, or a failed EGR valve solenoid.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 27 FMI 11?
 
Short distances may be possible but without electrical function the EGR valve cannot operate and a derate condition is likely to follow.
 
 
Will SPN 27 FMI 11 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If the ECM cannot control the EGR valve due to a circuit fault it will trigger derate conditions to protect the engine and limit emissions.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 27 FMI 11?
 
Inspect and repair the EGR valve wiring and connector. Test the solenoid and replace the valve if faulty. Once the ECM confirms correct electrical function of the EGR valve circuit the code should clear.

dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 11 – EGR Valve Circuit Fault
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 11 indicates an electrical circuit fault at the EGR valve. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the ECM has detected an abnormal electrical condition in the EGR valve control circuit, preventing proper valve operation and affecting exhaust gas recirculation control.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
EGR or emissions warning light illuminated 
Rough idle or unstable engine operation 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate possible Increased 
NOx emissions 
May appear alongside other EGR related codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects an electrical fault in the EGR valve circuit. Common causes include:
Open or short circuit in the EGR valve wiring harness 
Corroded or damaged EGR valve connector 
Failed EGR valve solenoid or actuator motor 
Water intrusion at the EGR valve connector 
Chafed or broken wiring between ECM and EGR valve 
Failed ECM output driver for the EGR valve circuit 
Poor ground connection at the EGR valve
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but without proper electrical function the EGR valve cannot be controlled by the ECM. This affects combustion efficiency and emissions control and a derate condition is likely to follow if the fault is not resolved.
Recommended Action
Inspect the EGR valve wiring harness and connector for damage, corrosion, or water intrusion. Check for broken or chafed wires between the ECM and EGR valve. Test the EGR valve solenoid resistance against specification. If wiring and solenoid test correctly have the ECM output circuit evaluated by a qualified diesel technician.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 11 mean?
 
It means the ECM has detected an electrical circuit fault at the EGR valve, preventing proper control of exhaust gas recirculation.
 
 
What causes SPN 27 FMI 11?
 
The most common causes are an open or short circuit in the EGR valve wiring, a corroded connector, water intrusion at the connector, or a failed EGR valve solenoid.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 27 FMI 11?
 
Short distances may be possible but without electrical function the EGR valve cannot operate and a derate condition is likely to follow.
 
 
Will SPN 27 FMI 11 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If the ECM cannot control the EGR valve due to a circuit fault it will trigger derate conditions to protect the engine and limit emissions.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 27 FMI 11?
 
Inspect and repair the EGR valve wiring and connector. Test the solenoid and replace the valve if faulty. Once the ECM confirms correct electrical function of the EGR valve circuit the code should clear.

Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 9 – EGR Valve Position Error (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 9 indicates that the EGR valve position is not matching the commanded position from the ECM. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the exhaust gas recirculation system is not responding correctly, which can affect emissions control, engine performance, and combustion efficiency.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
EGR or emissions warning light illuminated 
Rough idle or unstable engine operation 
Reduced engine performance Engine derate possible Increased 
NOx emissions 
Black smoke from exhaust possible
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects a discrepancy between the commanded EGR valve position and the actual position reported by the valve sensor. Common causes include:
Excessive carbon deposits in the EGR system
Carbon buildup on the EGR valve preventing proper movement
Stuck or seized EGR valve
Failed EGR valve position sensor
Damaged EGR valve actuator motor
Wiring or connector fault at the EGR valve
EGR cooler restriction affecting valve operation
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but an EGR valve position error affects combustion efficiency and emissions control. Engine performance will be impacted and a derate condition may follow if the fault persists. Address this promptly to avoid further carbon buildup or component damage.
Recommended Action
Inspect the EGR valve for carbon buildup and clean if necessary. Check the valve actuator and position sensor for proper operation. Inspect wiring and connectors at the EGR valve for damage or corrosion. If cleaning does not resolve the issue the EGR valve assembly may need to be replaced.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 27 FMI 9 mean?
 
It means the EGR valve is not moving to the position commanded by the ECM, indicating a mechanical, electrical, or carbon buildup issue with the valve or its control system.
 
 
What causes SPN 27 FMI 9?
 
The most common causes are carbon buildup preventing valve movement, a stuck or seized EGR valve, a failed position sensor, or a wiring fault at the valve connector.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 27 FMI 9?
 
Short distances may be possible but EGR valve position errors affect combustion and emissions control. A derate condition may follow if not addressed promptly.
 
 
Will SPN 27 FMI 9 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If the ECM cannot control EGR valve position correctly it will trigger derate conditions to limit emissions and protect the engine.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 27 FMI 9?
 
Clean or replace the EGR valve and inspect the position sensor and wiring. Once the valve responds correctly to ECM commands and position feedback matches commanded values the code should clear.

field_evidence.excerpt: The International MaxxForce DT 9 engine from 2014 can experience low power problems accompanied by the SPN 1209 FMI 4 diagnostic code. SPN_4257.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

field_evidence.title: Cummins ISB No Start Issue with SPN 1347 FMI 3 Code
field_evidence.excerpt: The Cummins ISB engine can experience a no start condition associated with the SPN 1347 FMI 3 fault code. This code indicates a fuel system issue that is often related to the fuel pump actuator or its wiring. Common problems with ISB engines include water in fuel sensor faults and fuel pump actuator failures, both of which can contribute to this no start condition. Even after replacing components like the water separator and fuel filter, problems such as poor injector control or faulty actuator signals may still cause symptoms like low idle and engine stalling. To address this issue, it is important to check the voltage and ground connections at the fuel pump actuator and inspect the wiring harness for any damage. Testing the actuator’s mechanical function is also a useful diagnostic step.

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 3936 FMI 1 – DEF Level Low
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3936 FMI 1 – DEF Level Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3936 FMI 1 indicates that the Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) level in the tank has dropped below the minimum threshold. This code commonly appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and will trigger derate conditions if DEF is not added promptly.
Symptoms
DEF warning light illuminated 
Check engine light on 
Audible warning chime 
Engine derate may begin if DEF level continues to drop
Cause
This code is triggered when the DEF level sensor detects fluid below the minimum required level. Common causes include normal DEF consumption without refilling, a slow DEF leak, or a faulty DEF level sensor giving a false low reading.
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but the engine will begin to derate — typically reducing power to 55 mph or less — if DEF is not added. Continued operation without addressing the code can result in a complete engine derate to 5 mph.
Recommended Action
Add DEF fluid immediately. If the warning clears after refilling, no further action is required. If the code persists after filling the tank, have the DEF level sensor and wiring inspected for faults.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3936 FMI 1 mean?
 
It means the DEF tank level has dropped below the minimum required threshold and the engine is at risk of entering a derate condition.
 
 
What causes SPN 3936 FMI 1?
 
Most commonly, the DEF tank simply needs to be refilled. It can also be caused by a DEF leak or a faulty DEF level sensor.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3936 FMI 1?
 
You can drive short distances but the engine will progressively derate if DEF is not added. Do not ignore this code.
 
 
Will SPN 3936 FMI 1 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Detroit Diesel engines are programmed to derate engine power and eventually limit speed to 5 mph if DEF level remains critically low.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3936 FMI 1?
 
Add DEF to the tank to bring it above the minimum level. The code should clear on its own once the sensor reads an acceptable level. If it persists, inspect the DEF level sensor.
 
 
Related codes

SPN 520372 FMI 16 
SPN 4334 FMI 18

← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 1569 FMI 31 indicates an engine protection derate condition. The ECM has limited engine power to protect critical components due to an active fault.
Symptoms
Reduced engine power
Limited vehicle speed
Check engine light illuminated
Possible shutdown warning
Cause
SPN 1569 FMI 31 is typically triggered when a critical engine fault has occurred. This may include high coolant temperature, low oil pressure, aftertreatment system issues, or DEF system faults.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Will SPN 1569 FMI 31 clear on its own once the engine cools down?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The derate condition may clear if a temperature-related trigger drops back within range, but the underlying problem will likely cause the code to return under similar operating conditions. Clearing codes without repairing the root cause is not a solution.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 1569 FMI 31 appear without any other fault codes?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: It's uncommon but possible if the triggering code was already cleared or if the protection activated from a parameter that was briefly out of range. In those cases, reviewing freeze-frame data and inactive code history in Cummins Insite is important.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does engine protection derate indicate the engine is already damaged?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Not necessarily �?the system is designed to prevent damage by reducing load before a threshold that would cause harm. Whether damage occurred depends on how long and how severely the protected condition was present. A shop inspection is warranted to assess component condition.

field_evidence.title: 2016 Freightliner Cascadia Forced Regen Failure SPN 4077 FMI 14
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2016 Freightliner Cascadia can experience forced regeneration failures indicated by the diagnostic trouble code SPN 4077 FMI 14. This issue generally relates to problems with the dosing block or injector during the forced regen process. Common problems in the Cascadia include forced regen interruptions and malfunctioning injector dosing blocks, which contribute to incomplete regeneration cycles. Even after replacing components such as the doser block and the 7th injector, carbon buildup may still cause the regen to fail. To address this issue, it is important to thoroughly clean the injectors and carefully inspect the wiring harnesses for any damage or poor connections. Additionally, verifying that the regen system’s sensors and pressure lines are clear helps maintain proper function.

field_evidence.title: 2017 Cascadia DD15: Diagnosing SPN-3510 and SPN-723 Engine Codes
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2017 Cascadia DD15 engine can experience specific issues indicated by engine fault codes SPN-3510 and SPN-723. Detroit Diesel SPN 4375 FMI 18 – DEF Doser Valve Response Fault (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4375 FMI 18 indicates that the DEF doser valve is not responding as commanded by the ECM. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the aftertreatment system cannot accurately control DEF delivery to the SCR catalyst, which will affect emissions performance and can lead to a derate condition if not resolved.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition possible 
Reduced aftertreatment system performance 
May appear alongside other DEF dosing related codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM sends a command to the DEF doser valve and does not receive the expected response. Common causes include:
Stuck or seized doser valve due to DEF crystallization 
Electrical fault at the doser valve solenoid 
Damaged or corroded wiring harness to the valve 
Failed doser valve unable to open or close correctly 
DEF contamination causing valve to stick 
ECM communication fault with the doser valve circuit
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but without proper doser valve response the SCR system cannot control DEF delivery accurately. The engine will likely enter a derate condition if the fault persists. Address this promptly to prevent further aftertreatment damage.
Recommended Action
Inspect the DEF doser valve for signs of crystallization or physical damage. Check the valve wiring and connector for corrosion or damage. If the valve is crystallized it may be cleanable but replacement is often the more reliable fix. Have the valve solenoid tested for proper electrical response before condemning the part.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4375 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the DEF doser valve is not responding correctly to ECM commands, preventing accurate control of DEF delivery to the SCR catalyst.
 
 
What causes SPN 4375 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are a stuck or crystallized doser valve, an electrical fault at the valve solenoid, or damaged wiring in the doser valve circuit.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4375 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but without proper doser valve function the SCR system cannot operate correctly and a derate condition is likely to follow.
 
 
Will SPN 4375 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If the ECM cannot control DEF dosing through the valve the SCR system will fail to meet emissions thresholds and a derate will be triggered.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4375 FMI 18?
 
Inspect, clean, or replace the DEF doser valve and verify wiring integrity. Once the valve responds correctly to ECM commands and the SCR system confirms proper DEF delivery the code should clear.

SPN 4094 FMI 18 
SPN 3362 FMI 1 
SPN 3363 FMI 16

field_evidence.title: 2009 Freightliner Cascadia Intake Air Pressure Sensor Code SPN 3563 FMI 4
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2009 Freightliner Cascadia frequently experiences issues related to the intake air pressure sensor, which can lead to engine performance problems. One common diagnostic code encountered is SPN 3563 FMI 4, which specifically points to a low or shorted voltage condition from the Engine Intake Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor. This sensor code can stem from several underlying causes. Damage or corrosion in the MAP sensor wiring harness may disrupt voltage signals. Additionally, leaks in the intake manifold can alter sensor accuracy, contributing to faults. Voltage irregularities detected on the sensor output are often an indicator of these issues. To address Code SPN 3563 FMI 4, it is advisable to inspect the MAP sensor wiring harness thoroughly for any signs of wear or corrosion.

field_evidence.excerpt: The 2013 Freightliner Cascadia is known to experience pressure limiting valve failures, particularly indicated by the diagnostic code SPN 679-FMI 7. This fault code signals that the pressure limiting valve is failing to close properly, which can result in a noticeable loss of power once the engine warms up. This issue in Cascadia models often stems from the valve's inability to regulate pressure as expected. However, replacing the valve alone does not always resolve the problem. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 23: Urge to Move Brake Switch Signal
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission may be configured with the Urge to Move (UTM) feature. If enabled and the transmission is in gear, UTM allows the vehicle to start moving after the vehicle service brake is released without having to depress the accelerator pedal. The UTM feature requires a primary on/off brake switch signal and one of two secondary brake signal messages to function. The brake signal messages are broadcast via J1939 to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).

dd_procedures.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives the vehicle’s Engine Speed message over the Primary Data Link and Secondary Engine Speed message over the Secondary Data Link. The TCM uses the Engine Speed as the primary engine speed message during normal transmission operation. If the Engine Speed becomes unavailable, the Secondary Engine Speed allows the transmission to operate in a degraded mode.

SPN_1073.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3480 FMI 16 - DPF Ash Load High
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3480 FMI 16 – DPF Ash Load High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3480 FMI 16 indicates that the ash load inside the Diesel Particulate Filter has accumulated beyond the acceptable threshold. Unlike soot, ash is a non-combustible byproduct of engine oil consumption and cannot be removed through regeneration. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and typically means the DPF requires professional cleaning or replacement.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF warning light illuminated 
Reduced engine performance 
Increased exhaust back pressure 
Regeneration cycles becoming more frequent 
Engine derate possible Regen completing but codes returning quickly
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM calculates that ash accumulation inside the DPF has exceeded the acceptable level based on engine hours and oil consumption data. Common causes include:
Normal long term ash accumulation over high mileage 
Excessive engine oil consumption accelerating ash buildup 
Wrong engine oil specification causing higher ash content 
Worn piston rings or valve seals increasing oil burning 
Extended oil change intervals contributing to higher ash deposits 
DPF approaching end of service life
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but ash cannot be burned off through regeneration like soot can. The DPF will continue to restrict exhaust flow as ash builds up, leading to increased back pressure, more frequent regens, and eventual derate. The DPF needs to be cleaned or replaced to resolve this condition.
Recommended Action
Have the DPF removed and professionally cleaned using a DPF cleaning machine to remove ash deposits. If the filter is too heavily loaded or damaged it will need to be replaced. Also investigate engine oil consumption — if the engine is burning excessive oil the root cause should be addressed to prevent rapid ash reaccumulation after cleaning.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3480 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the DPF has accumulated too much ash, which is a non-combustible byproduct of oil combustion that cannot be removed through normal regeneration and requires professional cleaning or filter replacement.
 
 
What causes SPN 3480 FMI 16?
 
The most common cause is normal long term ash accumulation over high mileage. Excessive engine oil consumption, wrong oil specification, or worn piston rings can accelerate ash buildup significantly.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3480 FMI 16?
 
Short distances may be possible but ash accumulation will not improve on its own. Continued operation will lead to increased back pressure, more frequent regeneration cycles, and eventual derate.
 
 
Will SPN 3480 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. As ash continues to restrict exhaust flow through the DPF the ECM will trigger derate conditions due to excessive back pressure and reduced aftertreatment performance.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3480 FMI 16?
 
The DPF must be removed and professionally cleaned or replaced. Simply performing a regeneration will not remove ash. Once the cleaned or new filter is reinstalled and the ECM confirms acceptable ash and back pressure levels the code should clear.

SPN 3719 FMI 0 
SPN 3251 FMI 18 
SPN 5246 FMI 0

Detroit Diesel SPN 3480 FMI 16 – DPF Ash Load High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3480 FMI 16 indicates that the ash load inside the Diesel Particulate Filter has accumulated beyond the acceptable threshold. Unlike soot, ash is a non-combustible byproduct of engine oil consumption and cannot be removed through regeneration. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and typically means the DPF requires professional cleaning or replacement.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF warning light illuminated 
Reduced engine performance 
Increased exhaust back pressure 
Regeneration cycles becoming more frequent 
Engine derate possible Regen completing but codes returning quickly
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM calculates that ash accumulation inside the DPF has exceeded the acceptable level based on engine hours and oil consumption data. Common causes include:
Normal long term ash accumulation over high mileage 
Excessive engine oil consumption accelerating ash buildup 
Wrong engine oil specification causing higher ash content 
Worn piston rings or valve seals increasing oil burning 
Extended oil change intervals contributing to higher ash deposits 
DPF approaching end of service life
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but ash cannot be burned off through regeneration like soot can. The DPF will continue to restrict exhaust flow as ash builds up, leading to increased back pressure, more frequent regens, and eventual derate. The DPF needs to be cleaned or replaced to resolve this condition.
Recommended Action
Have the DPF removed and professionally cleaned using a DPF cleaning machine to remove ash deposits. If the filter is too heavily loaded or damaged it will need to be replaced. Also investigate engine oil consumption — if the engine is burning excessive oil the root cause should be addressed to prevent rapid ash reaccumulation after cleaning.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3480 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the DPF has accumulated too much ash, which is a non-combustible byproduct of oil combustion that cannot be removed through normal regeneration and requires professional cleaning or filter replacement.
 
 
What causes SPN 3480 FMI 16?
 
The most common cause is normal long term ash accumulation over high mileage. Excessive engine oil consumption, wrong oil specification, or worn piston rings can accelerate ash buildup significantly.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3480 FMI 16?
 
Short distances may be possible but ash accumulation will not improve on its own. Continued operation will lead to increased back pressure, more frequent regeneration cycles, and eventual derate.
 
 
Will SPN 3480 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. As ash continues to restrict exhaust flow through the DPF the ECM will trigger derate conditions due to excessive back pressure and reduced aftertreatment performance.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3480 FMI 16?
 
The DPF must be removed and professionally cleaned or replaced. Simply performing a regeneration will not remove ash. Once the cleaned or new filter is reinstalled and the ECM confirms acceptable ash and back pressure levels the code should clear.

field_evidence.title: 2009 Freightliner Cascadia Intake Air Pressure Sensor Code SPN 3563 FMI 4
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2009 Freightliner Cascadia frequently experiences issues related to the intake air pressure sensor, which can lead to engine performance problems. One common diagnostic code encountered is SPN 3563 FMI 4, which specifically points to a low or shorted voltage condition from the Engine Intake Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor. This sensor code can stem from several underlying causes. Damage or corrosion in the MAP sensor wiring harness may disrupt voltage signals. Additionally, leaks in the intake manifold can alter sensor accuracy, contributing to faults. Voltage irregularities detected on the sensor output are often an indicator of these issues. To address Code SPN 3563 FMI 4, it is advisable to inspect the MAP sensor wiring harness thoroughly for any signs of wear or corrosion.

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 3720 FMI 16 – DPF Soot Load Percent High
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
SPN 3720 FMI 16 – DPF Soot Load Percent High
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3720 FMI 16 indicates that the calculated soot load percentage inside the Diesel Particulate Filter has exceeded the acceptable threshold. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and represents the ECM’s percentage based calculation of DPF soot loading. When this percentage rises above acceptable limits regeneration is required to prevent derate conditions and potential DPF damage.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or regen warning light illuminated 
Regeneration request active Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate possible if soot percentage continues to rise 
May appear alongside DPF differential pressure codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM calculates the DPF soot load percentage has risen above the acceptable threshold based on differential pressure readings and engine operating data. Common causes include:
Frequent short trips preventing passive regeneration 
Excessive idling not allowing exhaust temperatures to reach regen levels 
Failed or incomplete active regeneration cycles 
Faulty DPF differential pressure sensor affecting soot calculations 
Engine running rich causing accelerated soot production 
Regen inhibit switch preventing regeneration cycles 
Partially clogged DPF reducing regen effectiveness
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but soot load percentage will continue to rise without a successful regeneration. A parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible to prevent escalation to a more severe derate condition.
Recommended Action
Perform a parked regeneration as soon as possible ensuring the inhibit switch is off and fuel level is adequate. If the regen completes successfully and the code clears monitor for recurrence. If soot load percentage continues to rise after successful regens have the DPF differential pressure sensor, engine fueling system, and DPF condition inspected.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3720 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the ECM has calculated that the percentage of soot accumulated inside the DPF has exceeded the acceptable threshold and regeneration is required to prevent further escalation.
 
 
What causes SPN 3720 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are frequent short trips, excessive idling, failed regeneration cycles, a faulty differential pressure sensor, or engine conditions causing excessive soot production.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3720 FMI 16?
 
Short distances are possible but a parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible to reduce soot load percentage before more severe codes and derate conditions develop.
 
 
Will SPN 3720 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes if soot load percentage continues to rise without a successful regeneration the ECM will trigger progressive derate conditions to protect the DPF.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3720 FMI 16?
 
Perform a successful parked regeneration to reduce soot load percentage. The code should clear once the ECM calculates soot has dropped below the threshold. If it returns frequently investigate the underlying cause of excessive soot accumulation.
