dd_procedures.title: SPN 4360 FMI 18 - Aftertreatment SCR Inducement Active
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4360 FMI 18 – Aftertreatment SCR Inducement Active (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4360 FMI 18 indicates that the SCR inducement system has been activated on the engine. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and is the ECM’s way of enforcing compliance with emissions requirements by progressively limiting engine performance when the SCR system has been operating outside acceptable parameters for an extended period.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
SCR and DEF warning lights illuminated 
Significant engine derate active 
Vehicle speed may be limited 
Multiple SCR and NOx related codes likely present 
Engine power noticeably reduced
Cause
SCR inducement is triggered after the ECM has detected ongoing SCR system issues that have not been addressed within the allowed timeframe. Common causes include:
Extended operation with low or empty DEF tank 
Prolonged SCR efficiency faults left unresolved 
Repeated DEF quality faults not corrected 
DEF dosing system failure over extended period 
Tampered or missing SCR components 
Accumulated fault counts exceeding ECM thresholds
Can You Keep Driving?
The engine is already in an active derate condition with this fault. Vehicle speed and power will be significantly restricted. This fault will not resolve on its own and requires diagnosis and repair by a qualified diesel technician. Continued operation in this condition risks further aftertreatment damage.
Recommended Action
This fault requires professional diagnosis as it indicates a history of unresolved SCR system issues rather than a single component failure. Have a technician perform a full aftertreatment system evaluation including DEF quality, dosing system, NOx sensors, and SCR catalyst condition. Simply clearing codes without repair will not resolve the inducement condition.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4360 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the ECM has activated the SCR inducement system after detecting prolonged SCR system non-compliance, resulting in a significant engine derate condition to enforce emissions requirements.
 
 
What causes SPN 4360 FMI 18?
 
This fault is typically caused by extended operation with unresolved SCR system issues such as low DEF, poor DEF quality, or ongoing SCR efficiency faults that were not addressed within the ECM allowed timeframe.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4360 FMI 18?
 
The engine is already in active derate with this fault. Continued operation without repair will not improve the situation and risks further damage to the aftertreatment system.
 
 
Will SPN 4360 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. SCR inducement is specifically designed to enforce a derate condition and will continue until the underlying SCR system issues are properly diagnosed and repaired.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4360 FMI 18?
 
The underlying SCR system faults must be diagnosed and repaired by a qualified technician. Clearing codes without fixing the root cause will result in the inducement condition returning. A full aftertreatment system evaluation is required.

This fault will not resolve on its own and requires diagnosis and repair by a qualified diesel technician. Continued operation in this condition risks further aftertreatment damage.
Recommended Action
This fault requires professional diagnosis as it indicates a history of unresolved SCR system issues rather than a single component failure. Have a technician perform a full aftertreatment system evaluation including DEF quality, dosing system, NOx sensors, and SCR catalyst condition. Simply clearing codes without repair will not resolve the inducement condition.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4360 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the ECM has activated the SCR inducement system after detecting prolonged SCR system non-compliance, resulting in a significant engine derate condition to enforce emissions requirements.
 
 
What causes SPN 4360 FMI 18?
 
This fault is typically caused by extended operation with unresolved SCR system issues such as low DEF, poor DEF quality, or ongoing SCR efficiency faults that were not addressed within the ECM allowed timeframe.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4360 FMI 18?
 
The engine is already in active derate with this fault. Continued operation without repair will not improve the situation and risks further damage to the aftertreatment system.
 
 
Will SPN 4360 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. SCR inducement is specifically designed to enforce a derate condition and will continue until the underlying SCR system issues are properly diagnosed and repaired.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4360 FMI 18?
 
The underlying SCR system faults must be diagnosed and repaired by a qualified technician. Clearing codes without fixing the root cause will result in the inducement condition returning. A full aftertreatment system evaluation is required.

field_evidence.title: 2014 Freightliner Cascadia DD15 SPN 70 FMI 19 Engine Code Explained
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Freightliner Cascadia equipped with the DD15 engine may display the SPN 70 FMI 19 engine code, which relates to a turbocharger boost pressure fault. This problem is commonly associated with issues affecting the engine's turbocharger system. Such turbocharger boost pressure faults can stem from several causes. Notably, a faulty Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor may trigger this code. Additionally, boost leaks in hoses or intercooler connections and a malfunctioning wastegate actuator contribute to this problem. These issues can lead to engine derate or reduced performance if not addressed promptly. field_evidence.title: 2014 Freightliner Cascadia SPN 70 FMI 14 Parking Brake Switch Issue
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Freightliner Cascadia can encounter specific transmission-related problems, notably the SPN 70 FMI 14 code that signals an issue with the parking brake switch circuit. This fault impacts the automatic high idle feature of the vehicle. This parking brake switch fault can stem from wiring issues within the circuit, particularly after repair work on the CPC unit. To address this, it is important to verify the connections of the wiring harness at both the parking brake switch and the CPC module. Additionally, inspecting connectors for damage or corrosion is essential to ensure reliable operation. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 21 - Auto Neutral Park Brake Switch
dd_procedures.overview: An auto neutral feature is provided with this transmission which forces the transmission into neutral in all instances when the parking brake is applied. The OEM installs a normally closed T pressure switch into the existing air line to the parking brake valve. The pressure switch output and return wires are connected to the vehicle interface transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) connector. Consult OEM for switch location. This fault code indicates a failure of the switch that reports engagement of the park brake. When troubleshooting an Inactive code See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"

causes: This fault commonly appears during ECM software updates or after GPS signal loss in telematics-equipped vehicles
The ECM cannot determine why time synchronization has failed, creating uncertainty in data logging timestamps
Fleet operators frequently encounter this code when vehicles operate in GPS-denied environments or experience communication module malfunctions affecting time reference sources
RTC Chip Failure: Internal silicon defect in the real-time clock integrated circuit on the ECM board
ECM Power Loss: Backup battery or supercapacitor voltage drops below 2.0V, corrupting hour register
Software Corruption: Firmware update interrupted or incorrect calibration file loaded for time zone handling
Oscillator Drift: 32.768 kHz crystal aged or damaged, causing the RTC to count hours incorrectly
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM microcontroller monitors the RTC hour register via an I²C bus

dd_procedures.title: SPN 4353 FMI 18 - DEF Injection Quantity Low
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4353 FMI 18 – DEF Injection Quantity Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4353 FMI 18 indicates that the amount of DEF being injected into the exhaust stream is below the quantity required by the ECM to properly reduce NOx emissions. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and points to a problem within the DEF delivery system that will affect SCR performance and can trigger a derate condition if not resolved.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition possible 
Reduced SCR system efficiency 
May appear alongside other DEF dosing or pump related codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM determines that the actual DEF injection quantity is less than the commanded amount. Common causes include:
Worn or failing DEF pump not delivering adequate flow 
Clogged or partially blocked DEF dosing injector 
Low DEF level in tank Restricted DEF supply lines 
Faulty DEF metering valve Air in the DEF supply system 
DEF filter clogged restricting flow to injector
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but with insufficient DEF injection the SCR system cannot properly control NOx emissions. The engine will enter a derate condition if the delivery shortfall is not corrected. Do not ignore this code.
Recommended Action
Start by checking DEF tank level and refilling if low. Inspect the DEF filter and replace if clogged. Check DEF supply lines for restrictions or air ingestion points. If level and filter are good have the DEF pump output and dosing injector tested as wear or partial blockage in either component is a common cause of this fault.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4353 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the DEF system is injecting less fluid into the exhaust than the ECM requires to properly reduce NOx emissions through the SCR catalyst.
 
 
What causes SPN 4353 FMI 18?

dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4374 FMI 18 – DEF Doser Valve Current Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4374 FMI 18 indicates that the electrical current to the DEF doser valve is below the expected threshold. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and points to an electrical fault in the DEF dosing circuit that is preventing the doser valve from operating correctly, which will affect SCR system performance and can lead to a derate condition.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition possible 
DEF dosing system not functioning correctly 
May appear alongside other doser valve or DEF system codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects lower than expected current draw from the DEF doser valve circuit. Common causes include:
Open circuit in the doser valve wiring harness 
Damaged or corroded doser valve connector 
Failed doser valve solenoid with low resistance 
Broken wire between ECM and doser valve 
Water intrusion in the doser valve connector 
Faulty ECM output driver for the doser valve circuit
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but without proper electrical function the DEF doser valve cannot operate correctly and the SCR system will be unable to control DEF delivery. A derate condition is likely if the fault is not resolved promptly.
Recommended Action
Inspect the DEF doser valve wiring harness and connector for damage, corrosion, or broken wires. Check for water intrusion at the connector. Test the doser valve solenoid resistance against specification. If wiring and connector are intact and the solenoid tests good have the ECM output circuit evaluated by a qualified technician.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4374 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the electrical current to the DEF doser valve is below the expected level, indicating an electrical fault in the dosing circuit that prevents proper valve operation.
 
 
What causes SPN 4374 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are an open circuit or broken wire in the doser valve harness, a corroded connector, water intrusion at the connector, or a failed doser valve solenoid.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4374 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but without correct electrical supply the doser valve cannot function and the SCR system will be compromised, leading to a likely derate condition.
 
 
Will SPN 4374 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If the doser valve cannot operate due to low current the SCR system will be unable to deliver DEF correctly and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4374 FMI 18?
 
Inspect and repair the doser valve wiring and connector. Test the solenoid and replace the valve if faulty. Once the ECM confirms correct current draw to the doser valve the code should clear.

If enabled and the transmission is in gear, UTM allows the vehicle to start moving after the vehicle service brake is released without having to depress the accelerator pedal. The UTM feature requires a primary on/off brake switch signal and one of two secondary brake signal messages to function. The brake signal messages are broadcast via J1939 to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).

field_evidence.title: 2009 Freightliner Cascadia Intake Air Pressure Sensor Code SPN 3563 FMI 4
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2009 Freightliner Cascadia frequently experiences issues related to the intake air pressure sensor, which can lead to engine performance problems. One common diagnostic code encountered is SPN 3563 FMI 4, which specifically points to a low or shorted voltage condition from the Engine Intake Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor. This sensor code can stem from several underlying causes. Damage or corrosion in the MAP sensor wiring harness may disrupt voltage signals. Additionally, leaks in the intake manifold can alter sensor accuracy, contributing to faults. Voltage irregularities detected on the sensor output are often an indicator of these issues. To address Code SPN 3563 FMI 4, it is advisable to inspect the MAP sensor wiring harness thoroughly for any signs of wear or corrosion.

field_evidence.title: 2013 Freightliner Cascadia SPN 679-FMI 7 Pressure Valve Issue
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2013 Freightliner Cascadia is known to experience pressure limiting valve failures, particularly indicated by the diagnostic code SPN 679-FMI 7. This fault code signals that the pressure limiting valve is failing to close properly, which can result in a noticeable loss of power once the engine warms up. This issue in Cascadia models often stems from the valve's inability to regulate pressure as expected. However, replacing the valve alone does not always resolve the problem. Additional factors may contribute, such as potential faults within the electronic control module (ECM), wiring harness problems, or issues in the transmission control system and hydraulic pressure sensors. field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Freightliner Cascadia equipped with the DD15 engine may display the SPN 70 FMI 19 engine code, which relates to a turbocharger boost pressure fault. dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 - DPF Soot Load High
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 – DPF Soot Load High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 indicates that the Diesel Particulate Filter has accumulated soot beyond the moderate high threshold and requires regeneration. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and is a step above a routine regen request — if regeneration is not completed promptly the engine will enter a derate condition and the DPF may require forced regeneration or service.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or regen warning light illuminated 
Regen inhibited or unable to complete 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate possible 
Exhaust back pressure increased
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM calculates soot accumulation in the DPF has exceeded the moderate high threshold. Common causes include:
Frequent short trips preventing passive regeneration 
Excessive idling preventing exhaust temperatures from reaching regen levels 
Failed or incomplete active regeneration cycles 
Faulty DPF differential pressure sensor giving incorrect readings 
Clogged or damaged DPF requiring cleaning or replacement 
Engine running issues causing excessive soot production 
Regen inhibit switch left in the off position
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but soot load will continue to increase without a successful regeneration. The engine will enter a progressive derate condition if soot reaches critical levels. A parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible.
Recommended Action
Perform a parked regeneration as soon as possible. Ensure the regen inhibit switch is not active. If the parked regen completes successfully and the code clears, monitor for recurrence. If regen fails to complete or the code returns frequently, have the DPF differential pressure sensor, DPF condition, and engine fueling system inspected.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the DPF soot load has reached a high level and the engine requires a regeneration cycle to burn off accumulated soot before derate conditions are triggered.
 
 
What causes SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are frequent short trips, excessive idling, failed regeneration cycles, or a faulty DPF differential pressure sensor reporting incorrect soot levels.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
Short distances are possible but a parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible to prevent the code from escalating to a more severe derate condition.
 
 
Will SPN 3713 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If soot load continues to rise without a successful regeneration the ECM will trigger progressive derate conditions to protect the DPF from damage.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
Perform a successful parked regeneration. Once the DPF soot level drops below the threshold the code should clear. If it returns frequently have the DPF system and regeneration process inspected for underlying issues.
 
 
Related codes
SPN 3719 FMI 0 
SPN 3216 FMI 21 
SPN 5246 FMI 0 
SPN 1569 FMI 31

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3713 FMI 18 – DPF Soot Load Critical
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 18 – DPF Soot Load Critical (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 18 indicates that the Diesel Particulate Filter soot load has reached a critical level requiring immediate attention. This is a more severe version of the FMI 16 fault and appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines when soot accumulation has exceeded the point where normal regeneration may be sufficient. Immediate action is required to avoid severe derate or DPF damage.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF warning light illuminated 
Active derate condition 
Significantly reduced engine power

Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 – DPF Soot Load High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 indicates that the Diesel Particulate Filter has accumulated soot beyond the moderate high threshold and requires regeneration. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and is a step above a routine regen request — if regeneration is not completed promptly the engine will enter a derate condition and the DPF may require forced regeneration or service.
Symptoms

DPF or regen warning light illuminated 
Regen inhibited or unable to complete 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate possible 
Exhaust back pressure increased
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM calculates soot accumulation in the DPF has exceeded the moderate high threshold. Common causes include:
Frequent short trips preventing passive regeneration 
Excessive idling preventing exhaust temperatures from reaching regen levels 
Failed or incomplete active regeneration cycles 
Faulty DPF differential pressure sensor giving incorrect readings 
Clogged or damaged DPF requiring cleaning or replacement 
Engine running issues causing excessive soot production 
Regen inhibit switch left in the off position

Limited driving is possible but soot load will continue to increase without a successful regeneration. The engine will enter a progressive derate condition if soot reaches critical levels. A parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible.

Perform a parked regeneration as soon as possible. Ensure the regen inhibit switch is not active. If the parked regen completes successfully and the code clears, monitor for recurrence. If regen fails to complete or the code returns frequently, have the DPF differential pressure sensor, DPF condition, and engine fueling system inspected.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the DPF soot load has reached a high level and the engine requires a regeneration cycle to burn off accumulated soot before derate conditions are triggered.

The most common causes are frequent short trips, excessive idling, failed regeneration cycles, or a faulty DPF differential pressure sensor reporting incorrect soot levels.

Short distances are possible but a parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible to prevent the code from escalating to a more severe derate condition.
 
 
Will SPN 3713 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If soot load continues to rise without a successful regeneration the ECM will trigger progressive derate conditions to protect the DPF from damage.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
Perform a successful parked regeneration. Once the DPF soot level drops below the threshold the code should clear. If it returns frequently have the DPF system and regeneration process inspected for underlying issues.

field_evidence.title: Detroit DD15 Engine Trouble Code SPN 1176 Explained
field_evidence.excerpt: The Detroit DD15 engine can experience the trouble code SPN 1176, which indicates a turbocharger boost pressure fault. This issue relates specifically to the turbocharger system and its ability to maintain proper boost levels for engine performance. This turbocharger boost problem can stem from several potential causes. A faulty turbo actuator or boost sensor may trigger the fault code. Additionally, leaks in the intake system, such as loose hoses or damaged intercooler pipes, can contribute to incorrect boost pressure readings. Clogged exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valves can also affect engine performance and are related concerns to investigate. To address SPN 1176 effectively, inspect the turbo system for any leaks or component failures. Check hoses for looseness, examine intercooler

2: Selective Catalyst Reduction Outlet NOx Sensor – Error
Selective Catalyst Reduction Inlet NOx Sensor – Error

causes: Short to Ground: Sensor signal wire chafed against engine block or exhaust manifold causing direct ground contact
Failed O2 Sensor: Internal short circuit within the zirconia sensor element due to thermal stress or contamination
Harness Damage: Wiring insulation melted by exhaust heat or pinched during recent engine service or component replacement
ECM Fault: Internal driver failure in the ECM output stage, often seen after a voltage spike or reverse polarity event
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM monitors the O2 sensor heater circuit current using a precision shunt resistor
When current exceeds 2.5 A for more than 500 ms, the microcontroller sets FMI 6. The
Electrical analysis focuses on the sensor heater circuit and signal ground reference
A 0.5V offset caused by a corroded ground pin can push the signal into the ‘unknown’ zone

This problem is related to the Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) system, which plays a critical role in controlling emissions and maintaining engine performance. The SPN 5841 FMI 14 code indicates a fault specifically in the DEF dosing valve or injector. When this fault occurs, the engine automatically enters a derate mode as a protective measure to safeguard the emissions systems from damage. This derate issue can stem from blockages or faults within the DEF dosing valve, including electrical problems. To address the SPN 4357 code, practical steps include checking the DEF tank to verify sufficient fluid levels and inspecting the wiring harnesses connected to the DEF sensors for any damage. field_evidence.title: Freightliner Cascadia 2016: Understanding SPN 924 FMI 5 and SPN 523531 FMI 31 Codes
field_evidence.excerpt: The Freightliner Cascadia 2016 model often encounters engine sensor faults and communication errors that trigger specific fault codes. Two common codes are SPN 924 FMI 5 and SPN 523531 FMI 31, each pointing to distinct issues within the vehicle’s systems. SPN 924 FMI 5 indicates that the sensor data is out-of-range. This problem is frequently associated with the turbocharger or the boost pressure sensor. On the other hand, SPN 523531 FMI 31 relates to a communication loss with a control module, which can affect the overall operation of the vehicle's network. To address these faults, begin by inspecting the sensor wiring and connectors for any signs of damage or corrosion. Maintaining clean electrical connections is essential to prevent recurring faults. SPN_924.description_en: Auxiliary output #1 - data valid but below normal operating range (most severe level)
causes: Short to Ground: Output wire chafed against chassis or engine block, creating a direct ground path

Failed Actuator Coil: Internal winding short in relay or solenoid reduces resistance below 5 Ω. ECM Driver Damage: Overcurrent event has permanently degraded the internal MOSFET in the ECM. Corroded Connector: High resistance at pin 1 of the J1939 output connector causes voltage drop
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM continuously monitors the voltage at the Auxiliary Output #1 pin using a 12‑bit ADC sampled at 100 Hz
A reading below 2.5 V for more than 500 ms sets the active
This code can appear after ECM replacement or software updates
Technicians often encounter it when dealing with complex electrical systems in heavy machinery where auxiliary functions are critical
It requires a detailed analysis of electrical circuits and ECM logic to resolve, highlighting the importance of understanding both the machinery and its control systems
Technicians in workshops commonly employ oscilloscopes to trace signal paths and identify abnormalities

The TCM uses two vehicle J1939 data links to send and receive messages called the Primary Data Link and Secondary Data Link. The Primary Data Link is used by the TCM to communicate with the Engine, ABS, Body, and other vehicle ECUs during normal operation. The Secondary Data Link is used as a backup in the event that the Primary Data Link is inoperative. The Secondary Data Link is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton UltraShift SPN 1231 FMI 9 �?J1939 Network Communication Failure | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What diagnostic tool is used for Eaton UltraShift transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton ServiceRanger is the primary diagnostic software for UltraShift, Fuller Advantage, and Endurant transmissions. It provides fault code access, live data monitoring, and service routines. It can also identify which J1939 source address message is missing when SPN 1231 FMI 9 is active.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 1231 FMI 9 on an Eaton UltraShift cause it to lock in a single gear?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Depending on the TCM calibration and the severity of the communication loss, the transmission may default to a specific gear or a limited gear range rather than locking in a single ratio. The behavior varies by application and how critical the missing message is to the shift control algorithm.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the J1939 bus resistance check the same on Eaton UltraShift as on Allison or Detroit transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. The J1939 physical layer standard specifies 120-ohm terminating resistors at each end of the bus, resulting in approximately 60 ohms when measured between CAN High and CAN Low with all modules unpowered. This check is valid across all vehicles using the J1939 CAN standard regardless of manufacturer.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Mack mDrive SPN 1231 FMI 9 �?J1939 Network Communication Failure | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the Mack mDrive the same transmission as the Volvo I-Shift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. The Mack mDrive is essentially the same automated manual transmission as the Volvo I-Shift, badged for Mack trucks. The underlying transmission hardware, control software architecture, and J1939 communication protocols are closely related. VCADS Pro serves both Mack and Volvo platforms.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Will a failed engine EMS cause SPN 1231 FMI 9 on the Mack mDrive?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. If the engine EMS loses power or fails, the J1939 messages the mDrive TCM expects from the EMS will stop arriving, triggering SPN 1231 FMI 9. In this case, engine-related faults would also be present. Check all active codes in VCADS Pro to determine whether the communication loss is isolated to the transmission or is part of a broader network failure.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can corroded wiring cause intermittent SPN 1231 FMI 9 on the mDrive?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. Intermittent CAN bus communication faults are often caused by connector corrosion, partially damaged wiring, or loose terminating resistors that cause the bus resistance to vary. VCADS Pro may record the fault as inactive if the corrosion is not severe enough to cause a persistent loss of communication. Thorough connector cleaning and a wiring inspection under the truck are worthwhile steps for intermittent cases.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Volvo I-Shift SPN 1231 FMI 9 �?J1939 Network Communication Failure | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the Volvo I-Shift operate in manual mode if SPN 1231 FMI 9 is active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. The I-Shift typically falls back to a manual shift mode when J1939 communication with the engine EMS is lost, allowing the driver to select gears manually. Full automatic operation �?including automated clutch control and engine torque management during shifts �?requires intact J1939 communication.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the Volvo I-Shift J1939 network the same as the Mack mDrive?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The Volvo I-Shift and Mack mDrive are closely related �?the mDrive is the Mack-branded version of the I-Shift. The J1939 network architecture is essentially the same across both, and VCADS Pro or the equivalent Mack diagnostic tool is used for network diagnosis.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How do I test whether the CAN backbone or a branch harness is causing SPN 1231 FMI 9 on the I-Shift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: If multiple modules across the vehicle are reporting communication faults simultaneously, the CAN backbone or a terminating resistor is typically the cause. If only the I-Shift TCM is affected and other modules communicate normally, the fault is more likely in the branch harness from the backbone to the TCM connector. Resistance measurements and visual inspection of the specific harness branch can isolate the fault.

oem_troubleshooting.title: ZF AS-Tronic / TraXon SPN 1231 FMI 9 �?J1939 Network Communication Failure | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What diagnostic software is used for ZF AS-Tronic and TraXon transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: ZF TOOLBOX Plus (formerly ZTSE) is the primary diagnostic software for ZF AS-Tronic, TraXon, and EcoMat transmissions. It provides fault code access, live data monitoring, and service routines including identification of absent J1939 source addresses.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the J1939 network fault on a ZF AS-Tronic the same repair process as on an Eaton or Allison transmission?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The physical layer diagnosis is the same �?measure bus resistance, check terminating resistors, inspect wiring and connectors. The diagnostic software differs by brand, but the network architecture and failure modes are identical across J1939-compliant transmissions.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the ZF AS-Tronic or TraXon continue to operate in a manual mode if SPN 1231 FMI 9 is active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The ZF AS-Tronic and TraXon can typically operate in a manual shift fallback mode when J1939 communication is lost, allowing the driver to manually select gears. Full automatic operation requires the engine data provided over J1939, so full automation is restored only when the network communication is repaired.

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3362 FMI 1 – DEF Pump Pressure Low
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 – DEF Pump Pressure Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 indicates that the DEF pump is not generating enough pressure to properly supply the dosing system. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the SCR system cannot receive adequate DEF flow, which will affect emissions control and typically trigger a derate condition if left unresolved.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition 
Reduced engine performance 
SCR system unable to meet emissions thresholds 
Possible low DEF flow related codes appearing together
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects DEF pump pressure falling below the minimum required threshold. Common causes include:
Worn or failing DEF pump 
Low DEF level in tank 
Air in the DEF supply lines 
Clogged DEF filter restricting supply 
DEF line leak reducing system pressure 
Frozen DEF in cold weather conditions 
Faulty DEF pressure sensor
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but without adequate DEF pump pressure the dosing system cannot supply DEF to the SCR catalyst. The engine will enter a derate condition if the fault is not addressed. Do not ignore this code.
Recommended Action
Start by checking the DEF tank level and refilling if low. Inspect the DEF filter and replace if clogged. Check DEF lines for leaks or air ingestion points. If the level and filter are good, have the DEF pump tested and replaced if it is not generating adequate pressure.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 mean?
 
It means the DEF pump is not generating enough pressure to supply the dosing system, preventing the SCR system from properly controlling NOx emissions.
 
 
What causes SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
The most common causes are a worn or failing DEF pump, a clogged DEF filter, low DEF level, air in the supply lines, or a DEF line leak.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
Short distances may be possible but the engine will derate if the DEF system cannot supply adequate pressure to the dosing injector.
 
 
Will SPN 3362 FMI 1 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Without sufficient DEF pump pressure the SCR system cannot function and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
Check DEF level and filter first. If those are good, have the DEF pump tested and replaced if necessary. Once the system confirms adequate pressure and proper dosing the code should clear.

SPN 4076 FMI 18 
SPN 4094 FMI 18 
SPN 3936 FMI 1

SPN_3362.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_3362.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 17 - Start Enable Relay
dd_procedures.overview: The Start Enable Relay is wired into the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) on the coil side of the relay. At key on, the HCM determines which starting method to use (high-voltage Motor/Generator or Engine Starter). If the HCM uses the standard engine Starter, the 12-volt Cranking Relay is energized supplying battery power to the Start Enable Relay main feed, which then powers the Starter Solenoid.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 50 - J1939 Body Controller Message (HCM)
dd_procedures.overview: J1939 is a high-speed twisted pair 250K data link with one 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) connects to the J1939 data link at the 38-Way Connector. This link transmits information to the HCM and communicates with the other modules on the network such as the Body Controller.

dd_procedures.title: SPN 4094 FMI 18 – DEF Dosing Low Flow
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 18 – DEF Dosing Low Flow (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 18 indicates that the DEF dosing system is delivering less fluid than required to the SCR system. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the aftertreatment system cannot properly reduce NOx emissions, which will typically trigger a derate if not addressed.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate condition possible 
SCR system unable to meet emissions thresholds
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects insufficient DEF flow through the dosing system. Common causes include:
Clogged or failing DEF dosing injector 
DEF pump wear or failure 
Frozen or restricted DEF supply lines 
Low DEF level in tank Contaminated 
DEF blocking the dosing system 
Faulty DEF pressure sensor
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but the SCR system cannot function correctly without proper DEF dosing. The engine will likely enter a progressive derate condition if the fault is not resolved. Do not ignore this code.
Recommended Action
Start by checking the DEF tank level and fluid quality. If DEF is low or contaminated, refill or replace it. If the level is acceptable, have the DEF dosing injector, pump, and supply lines inspected for blockages or wear. A clogged dosing injector is a very common cause of this fault.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the DEF dosing system is not delivering enough fluid to the SCR system to properly reduce NOx emissions.
 
 
What causes SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are a clogged DEF dosing injector, a failing DEF pump, contaminated DEF fluid, or restricted DEF supply lines.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but the engine will likely derate if the dosing system cannot supply adequate DEF to the SCR system.
 
 
Will SPN 4094 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Without proper DEF dosing the SCR system cannot control NOx emissions and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
Inspect and address the root cause — typically a clogged dosing injector or DEF pump issue. Once the dosing system is flowing correctly and the SCR system confirms proper operation, the code should clear.
 
 
Related codes

SPN 3364 FMI 2
 
SPN 4334 FMI 16 
SPN 520372 FMI 16

field_evidence.excerpt: The 2022 Kenworth T680 automatic transmission may experience problems with gear shifting, specifically showing the diagnostic code SPN 525 FMI 12. This fault code points to an issue with the transmission’s intelligent device, which is often the Transmission Control Module (TCM) or its associated sensors. Intermittent gear engagement problems and transmission control module communication errors are among the common issues encountered with T680 trucks. These problems can stem from faults in the TCM or related electrical components and sensors affecting proper shift operations. To address this issue, it is important to inspect wiring harnesses and connectors for any signs of damage or corrosion. field_evidence.title: 2016 Freightliner Cascadia Evolution 125 SPN 525 Intermittent Code
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2016 Freightliner Cascadia Evolution 125 can experience an intermittent SPN 525 mechanical system code. This issue frequently appears alongside sensor communication glitches, especially when the vehicle is idling. Such codes indicate a fault within the mechanical system's sensor network. These conditions can disrupt sensor signals and cause intermittent code occurrences. This code points to a fault in the ABS wheel speed sensor circuit, which plays a crucial role in maintaining safe braking performance. Common wiring problems include corrosion, breaks, or loose connections that interfere with proper sensor operation. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 37: Power Connect
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with electronic components that require a high current. It is critical that the OEM power supply be able to deliver the proper voltage and current in these high-load situations for smooth and efficient shifting. Additional resistance introduced into the system can cause the supplied voltage to drop low enough to cause performance issues. Fault Code 37 indicates an excessive resistance between the power supply source (battery or starter) and the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).

SPN_627.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

field_evidence.excerpt: The MaxxForce 11/13 engines from model years 2010 to 2012 commonly experience crank no start problems linked to camshaft sensor signal loss. This issue is identified by the diagnostic code SPN 636 FMI 10, which points to a fault in the camshaft position sensor signal. A camshaft position sensor signal fault can cause the engine to fail to start because the Engine Control Module (ECM) relies on this signal to manage fuel injection and ignition timing. Without a proper camshaft signal, the ECM cannot properly control these critical engine functions, resulting in a no-start condition. To diagnose and address this issue, it is important to verify the integrity of the camshaft sensor wiring and ensure connectors are clean and secure. Once the PTO is engaged, the TCM receives a confirmation (input) that the PTO is engaged to complete the operation. The TCM can be configured to control the PTO with messages over the vehicle J1939 Data Link (J1939 controlled) and/or relay circuit hardwired directly to the TCM (Hardwire controlled). field_evidence.title: 2017 Peterbilt 579 Transmission Codes SPN-788 & SPN-3645 Explained
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2017 Peterbilt 579 is known to experience transmission shifting issues that often trigger fault codes such as SPN-788 and SPN-3645. These codes are typically associated with sensor or solenoid failures within the transmission system. Specifically, the SPN-788 code indicates a fault with the transmission output speed sensor. This sensor plays a crucial role in monitoring the speed of the transmission output shaft. Meanwhile, the SPN-3645 code relates to a malfunction of the gear shift solenoid, which is responsible for controlling the smooth engagement of gears during shifts. Addressing these issues involves several key checks. causes: Upon activation, the ECM engages a torque derate strategy, reducing maximum fuel injection quantity by up to 40% to limit peak cylinder pressure below 180 bar
On Bosch EDC17 systems, the engine speed is also capped at 1800 rpm
The fault remains active until the pressure drops below the threshold for 10 seconds and a manual reset is performed via
Sensor Short: Internal short to ground in the intake manifold pressure sensor, drawing excessive current
Harness Chafing: Wiring insulation worn through against metal brackets, causing a direct ground path
ECM Supply Fault: 5V reference supply inside ECM partially shorted, overloading the sensor circuit
Connector Corrosion: Moisture ingress in the sensor connector creating a low-resistance path to ground
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM microcontroller monitors the intake manifold pressure sensor signal line for current draw

dd_procedures.title: SPN 4076 FMI 18 – DEF Dosing Injector Fault
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4076 FMI 18 – DEF Dosing Injector Fault (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4076 FMI 18 indicates a fault with the DEF dosing injector, which is the component responsible for spraying DEF fluid into the exhaust stream ahead of the SCR catalyst. When this injector fails or becomes restricted on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines, the SCR system cannot properly reduce NOx emissions and a derate condition will follow.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition 
White residue or crystallization around the injector 
Reduced engine performance 
SCR system unable to meet emissions thresholds
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects the DEF dosing injector is not performing within specification. Common causes include:
Clogged or crystallized dosing injector from DEF deposits 
Failed or stuck dosing injector valve 
DEF injector electrical fault or wiring issue 
Restricted DEF supply to the injector 
Contaminated DEF causing injector blockage 
Failed return line preventing injector purge cycle
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but without a functioning dosing injector the SCR system cannot reduce NOx emissions. The ECM will trigger a progressive derate condition. This fault should be addressed promptly to avoid further damage to the aftertreatment system.
Recommended Action
Have the DEF dosing injector inspected for clogging, crystallization, or electrical faults. A clogged injector can sometimes be cleaned but is often more cost effective to replace. Also inspect the DEF return line to ensure the purge cycle is functioning correctly, as a blocked return line is a common contributing factor.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4076 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the DEF dosing injector is not operating correctly and the SCR system cannot properly inject DEF into the exhaust stream to reduce NOx emissions.
 
 
What causes SPN 4076 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are a clogged or crystallized DEF dosing injector, an electrical fault at the injector, or a blocked DEF return line preventing proper purging.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4076 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but the engine will derate without a functioning dosing injector. Address this fault as soon as possible.
 
 
Will SPN 4076 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. The ECM will trigger a derate condition when the dosing injector cannot supply DEF to the SCR system at the required rate.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4076 FMI 18?
 
Inspect, clean, or replace the DEF dosing injector and verify the return line is clear. Once the injector is functioning correctly and the SCR system confirms proper DEF dosing, the code should clear.
 
 
Related codes

SPN 3509 FMI 16 
SPN 4334 FMI 16 
SPN 3364 FMI 2

dd_procedures.title: SPN 1127 FMI 16 – Exhaust Back Pressure High
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 1127 FMI 16 – Exhaust Back Pressure High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 1127 FMI 16 indicates that exhaust back pressure has exceeded the acceptable operating threshold. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and signals that something is restricting exhaust flow through the aftertreatment system. Left unresolved high exhaust back pressure can reduce engine performance, damage the turbocharger, and lead to progressive derate conditions.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or aftertreatment warning light illuminated 
Reduced engine power and performance 
Engine derate condition possible 
Black smoke from exhaust Reduced fuel economy 
Turbocharger may be affected by restricted exhaust flow
Cause
This code triggers when the exhaust back pressure sensor detects pressure above the maximum acceptable threshold. Common causes include:
Heavily soot or ash loaded 
DPF restricting exhaust flow 
Collapsed or physically damaged DPF substrate 
Clogged or restricted exhaust system components 
Failed exhaust back pressure sensor giving false readings 
Blocked exhaust pipe or muffler 
Faulty exhaust brake stuck in closed position 
High ash accumulation reducing DPF flow capacity
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but high exhaust back pressure puts significant strain on the turbocharger and engine. Continued operation without addressing the restriction risks turbocharger damage and progressive engine derate. Attempt a parked regeneration and seek diagnosis promptly.
Recommended Action
Start by attempting a parked regeneration to reduce DPF soot load. If back pressure remains high after a successful regen inspect the exhaust system for physical blockages or damage. Check the exhaust brake if equipped to ensure it is not stuck closed. Have the DPF inspected for ash loading or substrate damage. If all components check out test the exhaust back pressure sensor for accuracy.
FAQ Q&As
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 1127 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means exhaust back pressure has exceeded the maximum acceptable threshold, indicating a restriction in the exhaust or aftertreatment system that is reducing engine performance.
 
 
What causes SPN 1127 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are a heavily loaded DPF, a collapsed or damaged DPF substrate, a blocked exhaust component, or a faulty exhaust back pressure sensor.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 1127 FMI 16?
 
Short distances may be possible but high back pressure puts strain on the turbocharger and engine. Address this fault promptly to avoid further damage.
 
 
Will SPN 1127 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If exhaust back pressure remains above acceptable levels the ECM will trigger derate conditions to protect the engine and turbocharger from damage.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 1127 FMI 16?
 
Perform a parked regeneration first. If pressure remains elevated inspect the exhaust system and DPF for blockages or damage. Once the restriction is resolved and back pressure returns to normal the code should clear.

SPN 3713 FMI 18 
SPN 3250 FMI 16 
SPN 3480 FMI 16

Detroit Diesel SPN 1127 FMI 16 indicates that exhaust back pressure has exceeded the acceptable operating threshold. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and signals that something is restricting exhaust flow through the aftertreatment system. Left unresolved high exhaust back pressure can reduce engine performance, damage the turbocharger, and lead to progressive derate conditions.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or aftertreatment warning light illuminated 
Reduced engine power and performance 
Engine derate condition possible 
Black smoke from exhaust Reduced fuel economy 
Turbocharger may be affected by restricted exhaust flow
Cause
This code triggers when the exhaust back pressure sensor detects pressure above the maximum acceptable threshold. Common causes include:
Heavily soot or ash loaded 
DPF restricting exhaust flow 
Collapsed or physically damaged DPF substrate 
Clogged or restricted exhaust system components 
Failed exhaust back pressure sensor giving false readings 
Blocked exhaust pipe or muffler 
Faulty exhaust brake stuck in closed position 
High ash accumulation reducing DPF flow capacity
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but high exhaust back pressure puts significant strain on the turbocharger and engine. Continued operation without addressing the restriction risks turbocharger damage and progressive engine derate. Attempt a parked regeneration and seek diagnosis promptly.
Recommended Action
Start by attempting a parked regeneration to reduce DPF soot load. If back pressure remains high after a successful regen inspect the exhaust system for physical blockages or damage. Check the exhaust brake if equipped to ensure it is not stuck closed. Have the DPF inspected for ash loading or substrate damage. If all components check out test the exhaust back pressure sensor for accuracy.
FAQ Q&As
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 1127 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means exhaust back pressure has exceeded the maximum acceptable threshold, indicating a restriction in the exhaust or aftertreatment system that is reducing engine performance.
 
 
What causes SPN 1127 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are a heavily loaded DPF, a collapsed or damaged DPF substrate, a blocked exhaust component, or a faulty exhaust back pressure sensor.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 1127 FMI 16?
 
Short distances may be possible but high back pressure puts strain on the turbocharger and engine. Address this fault promptly to avoid further damage.
 
 
Will SPN 1127 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If exhaust back pressure remains above acceptable levels the ECM will trigger derate conditions to protect the engine and turbocharger from damage.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 1127 FMI 16?
 
Perform a parked regeneration first. If pressure remains elevated inspect the exhaust system and DPF for blockages or damage. Once the restriction is resolved and back pressure returns to normal the code should clear.

field_evidence.title: 2013 Kenworth T660 Cummins ISX15 SPN862 Engine Light Issue
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2013 Kenworth T660 equipped with the Cummins ISX15 engine can experience an SPN862 engine light warning. This code points to a fault with the turbocharger boost pressure sensor. Common problems associated with this vehicle include clutch wear and excessive engine oil consumption, especially after heavy use or repairs. These issues may contribute to the engine sensor fault and trigger the SPN862 code. The sensor fault can stem from several factors. Clogged air filters reduce airflow and affect boost pressure readings, while faulty sensors themselves are a direct cause. Following a clutch replacement, vacuum leaks or damaged hoses may disrupt sensor signals. Additionally, damage to the turbocharger actuator or related wiring can impact sensor function. field_evidence.title: SPN 560 Code Diagnosis and Fix for Diesel Engines
field_evidence.excerpt: The SPN 560 code frequently appears in diesel engines and is often related to faults in the diesel particulate filter (DPF) pressure sensor or its associated wiring. These sensor issues or wiring problems can lead to intermittent engine warnings, affecting engine reliability and performance. This code specifically indicates a problem with the DPF pressure sensor or its circuit. Damage or corrosion in the sensor’s wiring harness is a common cause. Additionally, clogging of the DPF due to excessive soot buildup can also trigger the SPN 560 code. To address this issue, inspect the sensor’s wiring harness for any signs of damage or corrosion. field_evidence.excerpt: The ABS transmission fault identified as SPN 563 is a known issue that can limit the truck’s speed to 5 miles per hour when the engine runs at 2200 RPM. Faults such as damaged wiring, corroded connectors, or a malfunctioning sensor itself can trigger the SPN 563 code and result in the speed restriction. SPN_5848.pgn_description: This message contains aftertreatment intermediate ammonia information for aftertreatment system 1 (or bank 1).
causes: Sensor Element Degradation: NH3 sensor ceramic element contamination or thermal stress causing unstable resistance characteristics and signal drift
Wiring Harness Problems: Intermittent connector corrosion, damaged shielding, or loose terminals creating erratic electrical signal transmission patterns
ECM Software Corruption: Control module firmware issues preventing proper interpretation of NH3 sensor data and fault classification algorithms
Exhaust System Leaks: Air intrusion upstream of sensor causing false readings and confusing ECM
Sensor Internal Failure: NH3 sensor’s internal reference electrode or heater circuit has degraded beyond acceptable limits
CAN Bus Corruption: Short or open in CAN lines between sensor and ECM disrupts intelligent device communication
Supply Voltage Fault: Sensor supply voltage below 10V or above 16V during cranking or transient load conditions
ECM Software Mismatch: After ECM replacement, software calibration does not support the installed NH3 sensor revision
steps: Guide Visual Inspection: Check NH3 sensor harness for chafing, melting, or pinched wires near exhaust and frame rails. Resistance Test: Measure resistance between sensor signal and ground
Guide Verify sensor power: Check for 12V at sensor pin 1 and ground continuity at pin 2 with key-on, engine-off. Inspect CAN bus: Measure resistance between CAN_H and CAN_L at sensor connector
Guide Read Freeze Frame: Record engine speed, load, and exhaust temperature at fault onset to identify operating conditions. Verify DEF Quality: Test DEF concentration with a refractometer

This safety mode ensures controlled deceleration but can affect vehicle performance
Understanding the conditions triggering such responses helps in diagnosing underlying electrical issues and restoring normal operations effectively

SPN_1319.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_1319.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

steps: [FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.

SPN_19.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_19.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

SPN_380.name: Articulation Angle
SPN_380.description: SAE J1939 Heavy-Duty Diagnostic Parameter: Articulation Angle
SPN_380.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_380.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).
causes: Damaged sensor wiring: Chafed or broken wires in the harness between the articulation sensor and the chassis controller
Faulty sensor connector: Corroded or loose pins at the 3-pin DEUTSCH connector cause intermittent signal loss
Defective angle sensor: Internal Hall-effect element failure prevents the sensor from outputting a valid PWM signal
ECM software glitch: Firmware bug in the steering control module occasionally skips the message transmission slot
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM monitors the articulation angle message ID on the CAN bus at a 10 Hz rate
If no valid message is received for 1.2 seconds (12 consecutive missed updates), the FMI 9 is set
Technicians frequently encounter this fault on articulated dump trucks and wheel loaders during post-repair validation
steps: Guide Check CAN bus traffic: Connect a J1939 breakout box and verify the angle message ID appears every 100 ms ±10 ms. Inspect sensor connector: Unplug the 3-pin DEUTSCH connector
Guide Visual harness inspection: Examine wiring from sensor to ECM for cuts, chafing, or loose connectors at the pivot. Sensor resistance test: Measure between signal and ground pins

Guide Visual inspection: Check connector for bent pins, corrosion, or broken wire at articulation joint flex zone. Voltage measurement: Measure 5V reference and ground at sensor connector with ignition on. Signal sweep test: Monitor signal voltage while slowly articulating full left to right

If the hybrid system has a fault, or if a hybrid component is above the optimum operating temperature, the vehicle will reduce the amount of available Motor/Generator torque. Note: This symptom-based test should only be performed when directed by the Symptom-Driven Diagnostics Index and there are no Active fault codes.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can worn synchronizers on the ZF AS-Tronic be replaced without a full transmission overhaul?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: ZF AS-Tronic and TraXon transmissions can be repaired by qualified ZF-authorized service centers. Synchronizer ring replacement is possible as part of a targeted repair, though accessing the synchronizers requires significant disassembly. ZF Testman can identify the specific affected gear to guide the repair scope.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How does ZF Testman identify which gear is causing SPN 731 FMI 2 on the AS-Tronic?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: ZF Testman logs the gear number and shift event associated with each ratio mismatch fault occurrence. The fault history shows which specific gear consistently fails to achieve the correct ratio. This narrows the mechanical investigation to the actuator, synchronizer, and gear set associated with that particular position.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Will the ZF AS-Tronic or TraXon continue to drive if one gear has a ratio mismatch fault?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes, in most cases. The ZF TCU is designed to recognize a failed gear and adjust its shift strategy to avoid that gear if possible. The transmission will continue to operate with a reduced gear selection until the fault is repaired. Extended operation avoiding a gear does add load to adjacent gears and may accelerate wear.

causes: Worn synchronizer rings unable to match shaft speeds for engagement Shift actuator not completing the full stroke for gear engagement Low air supply pressure reducing actuator force Speed sensor providing inaccurate ratio data

SPN_751.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_751.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

dd_procedures.overview: This fault code indicates either an electrical or mechanical failure in the WetClutch system.
steps: A. Check WetClutch fluid level. Key on. Place the transmission in neutral. Allow engine to idle at 700-800 RPM for a minimum of 2 minutes. causes: Identify ECA installed on transmission. Inspect ECA OEM Power Supply Connector, reference image below. If equipped with a Gen1 ECA, Go to Step B If equipped with a Gen2 ECA, go to
steps: C. Perform a Load Test on each vehicle battery. Key off. Set parking brake and chock wheels. Load test each vehicle battery per OEM specifications. Record reading(s). Go to Step V If

I. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Determine which FMI set for Fault Code 64, as noted in Step B. If FMI 2 or 12 set and no fault was found with the ECA Power Supply Harness or battery/charging system, replace the Electronic Clutch Actuator (ECA) . Go to Step V If FMI 7 set, Go to Step J

D. Verify condition of 2-Way ECA Connector. Key off. Disconnect 2-Way Gen2 ECA Connector. Verify connector is free from any corrosion; the terminals are not bent, spread or loose; and there is no damage to the connector body. F. Verify polarity of battery voltage at ECA. Key off. Measure voltage between 2-Way Gen2 ECA Connector Pin 2 (Battery positive) and ground. Record reading(s) in table. Compare reading(s) in table. Use a sealed beam headlamp or blower motor attached to Pin 2 (Battery positive) and Pin 1 (Battery negative). Load Test for 5 minutes to verify the harness will carry a load with the 40-amp fuse or fusible link installed. Wiggle the ECA Power Supply Harness during the Load Test from the vehicle batteries to ECA. If the ECA Power Supply Harness does not carry a load, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement. Once the fault is active, the ABS ECU disables traction control and retarder intervention for axle 3 left

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 65: Gen1 ECA Speed Sensor
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with an Electronic Clutch Actuator (ECA) Speed Sensor that provides a secondary engine speed signal to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU). The ECA Speed Sensor is installed in the clutch housing. The ECA broadcasts the ECA Speed Sensor signal to the TECU through the High Integrity Link (HIL) contained within the transmission harness. The TECU uses the ECA Speed Sensor signal to determine engine speed when the J1939 engine speed signal is not available. Early models have a thread-in ECA Speed Sensor installed in the flywheel housing. Fau

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 345 Engine Speed
dd_procedures.overview: The Procision transmission is equipped with speed sensors to monitor Engine, Primary Input, Secondary Input, and Output speeds. The speed sensors provide rotational speed inputs to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of verifying Primary and Secondary Clutch engagement, making shift decisions, and confirming gear engagement. The Engine Speed Sensor is located on the Pump assembly and captures rotational speed from a pump mounted tone wheel. The Engine Speed Sensor is connected to the TCM through the Transmission Harness.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 54 - DC/DC Converter Output Voltage
dd_procedures.overview: The DC/DC Converter is connected to the Power Electronics Carrier (PEC), which provides 340 volts DC. The voltage is reduced to 12-volts DC and maintains the 12-volt system during engine off PTO operation. The DC/DC maintains a steady 14.2 (±0.2) volts output and increases the amperage with vehicle demand up to 1.5 kw or 120 amps. The DC/DC Converter also produces a feedback voltage from the 4-Way Connector. The voltage output is a 0–5 volt signal, which shows 5 volts when the Converter is at 14.2 (±0.2) volts on the output. If the Converter output drops, the feedback signal drops accordingly.

[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.

[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.
[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.

causes: Failing or degraded NOx sensor
NOx sensor contaminated by DEF crystallization
Exhaust leaks affecting sensor readings
Wiring or connector damage at the NOx sensor
Failed SCR catalyst causing abnormal NOx readings
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
steps: Have the NOx sensor and its wiring inspected first as sensor failure is the most common cause.
Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor location.
If the sensor and wiring check out, have the SCR catalyst evaluated as a degraded catalyst can produce abnormal NOx readings that trigger this rationality fault.

SPN_4138.name: ADP4 valve switch positive short circuit. If 'stuck' or a short circuit of one of these valves is wrongly reported as 'splitter disengagement', 'main gearbox gear shifting', 'main transmission gear shift engagement', 'main shut-off valve 1', 'clutch closing valve 2' or 'splitter clutch 1', the power cannot be switched off.

steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sıvı seviyelerini, emiş filtrelerini ve mekanik aşınma belirtilerini kontrol edin.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Aktüatör/solenoid bobin direncini ölçün ve soket kilit tırnaklarını kontrol edin.
[FMI 6 katalog] Bobin sargısında dahili izolasyon delinmesi veya aktüatör mekanik sıkışması kontrolü yapın.
[FMI 8 katalog] Osiloskop ile PWM sinyal doluluk oranını (Duty Cycle) ve gürültü seviyesini inceleyin.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör içindeki elemanın gevşediğini veya soket pini korozyonunu inceleyin.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.
[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.
SPN_7381.pgn_description: Contains command signals to Turbocharger Compressor Blowoff, Wastegate, Cylinder Head Bypass and Throttle Valve actuators.

steps: [FMI 9 katalog] Sensör veya kaynak modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claim) doğrulayın.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör içindeki elemanın gevşediğini veya soket pini korozyonunu inceleyin.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.
[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.
[FMI 18 katalog] Dozaj pompası, hava tahrik valfi veya debi kısıtlamalarını giderin.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.
[FMI 31 katalog] İlgili anahtar veya sensör kontak pozisyonunu doğrulayın.

steps: [FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Aktüatör/solenoid bobin direncini ölçün ve soket kilit tırnaklarını kontrol edin.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.

SPN_520219.description: ECU internal MIL lamp (OBD lamp) driver chip overtemperature

causes: FMI 2: Data erratic, intermittent or incorrect.

FMI 5: Current below normal or open circuit.

[FMI 6 katalog] Bobin sargısında dahili izolasyon delinmesi veya aktüatör mekanik sıkışması kontrolü yapın.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.

SPN_521316.name: Beam or antenna damage

fault_matrix.description: Data valid but below normal operational range
Data erratic, intermittent or incorrect
Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source
Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source
Current below normal or open circuit
Current above normal or grounded circuit
Mechanical system not responding properly
Abnormal frequency, pulse width or period
Abnormal update rate
Abnormal rate of change
Root cause not known
Bad intelligent device or component
Out of calibration
Special instructions

causes: FMI 1: Data valid but below normal operational range.
FMI 2: Data erratic, intermittent or incorrect.
FMI 3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source.
FMI 4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source.
FMI 5: Current below normal or open circuit.
steps: [FMI 1 katalog] Sıvı seviyelerini, emiş filtrelerini ve mekanik aşınma belirtilerini kontrol edin.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Aktüatör/solenoid bobin direncini ölçün ve soket kilit tırnaklarını kontrol edin.
[FMI 6 katalog] Bobin sargısında dahili izolasyon delinmesi veya aktüatör mekanik sıkışması kontrolü yapın.
[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.
[FMI 8 katalog] Osiloskop ile PWM sinyal doluluk oranını (Duty Cycle) ve gürültü seviyesini inceleyin.
[FMI 9 katalog] Sensör veya kaynak modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claim) doğrulayın.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör içindeki elemanın gevşediğini veya soket pini korozyonunu inceleyin.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.
SPN_521316.causes_source: SAE J1939-73 FMI fault matrix (DB fault_matrix, Tur-30 türetme)

SPN_522012.description: OBD-related fault for torque limitation of the urea injection control unit (DCU) activated
SPN_522012.description_en: OBD-related fault for torque limitation of the urea injection control unit (DCU) activated
causes: OBD-related fault for torque limitation of the urea injection control unit (DCU) activated.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sıvı seviyelerini, emiş filtrelerini ve mekanik aşınma belirtilerini kontrol edin.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.
[FMI 31 katalog] İlgili anahtar veya sensör kontak pozisyonunu doğrulayın.

SPN_522027.description: Downstream NOx sensor - NOxNO2CorCat2Ds CAN information outside SAE defined rational limits
SPN_522027.description_en: Downstream NOx sensor - NOxNO2CorCat2Ds CAN information outside SAE defined rational limits
causes: FMI 0: Data valid but above normal operational range.
FMI 1: Data valid but below normal operational range.
FMI 2: Data erratic, intermittent or incorrect.
FMI 3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source.
FMI 4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sıvı seviyelerini, emiş filtrelerini ve mekanik aşınma belirtilerini kontrol edin.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Aktüatör/solenoid bobin direncini ölçün ve soket kilit tırnaklarını kontrol edin.
[FMI 6 katalog] Bobin sargısında dahili izolasyon delinmesi veya aktüatör mekanik sıkışması kontrolü yapın.
[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.
[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.
[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.
[FMI 18 katalog] Dozaj pompası, hava tahrik valfi veya debi kısıtlamalarını giderin.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.
SPN_522027.causes_source: SAE J1939-73 FMI fault matrix (DB fault_matrix, Tur-30 türetme)
